docs.title: Resona
docs.text:
Modular audio transcription platform with pluggable ASR engines and a composable postprocessing pipeline. Designed for German medical dictation — usable for any language.

Works standalone (no server needed), against a self-hosted stack, or with cloud STT/TTS providers. Engines are discovered via Python entry points; postprocessing is a separate layer the engine never sees.

docs.title: Three paths to first transcription
docs.text:
Local-onlyDockerCloud

No server required. The CLI spawns the engine in-process.

uv tool install --from ./apps/resona-cli resona-cli
resona transcribe recording.mp3

Output is written next to the input file as .txt.

Full stack with job queue, persistence, and postprocessing.

docker compose -f docker-compose.resona.yml up
resona transcribe recording.mp3   # CLI auto-connects to :7000

Use a cloud STT provider — no GPU needed.

export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
resona transcribe recording.mp3 --engine openai

Get started →

docs.title: Stateless Engine Contract
docs.text: The engine server (resona-engine-server) is intentionally stateless. Understanding this constraint is the single most important thing to know before contributing to or extending Resona.

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
resona-engine-server has no database and no persistent state

Every request to the engine must be completely self-contained. The engine never reads from or writes to a database, never applies text replacements or LLM postprocessing, and never knows about jobs, prompts, or users.

docs.title: What the engine CAN do
docs.text:
• Load audio from the multipart request body
  • Run ASR inference against the loaded model
  • Return {text, language, segments} — raw transcript only

docs.title: What the engine CANNOT do
docs.text:
• Read from or write to any database
  • Apply text replacements or LLM postprocessing
  • Delete audio files
  • Know about jobs, initial prompts, or replacements stored elsewhere

docs.title: The design test
docs.text:
Before adding any feature to an engine or engine-server, apply this test:

The request-body test

"Can this be done using only what is in the HTTP request?"

If yes — it may belong in the engine. If it requires a database lookup or a postprocessing step — it belongs in resona-api or resona-postprocess.

docs.title: Why this separation matters
docs.text:
GPU machine vs API machine. The engine runs on a GPU host where inference is fast. The API runs on a lightweight host (or serverless container) with no GPU requirement. Keeping the engine stateless means you can scale, swap, or restart the GPU host without touching the API or any stored data.

Swappable engines. Because all engines expose the same HTTP interface, resona-api can switch between faster-whisper, whisper, voxtral, or a cloud provider without any code changes. The RESONA_ENGINE environment variable selects which plugin loads; the rest of the system is unaffected.

Testability. A stateless HTTP service is trivially mockable. Hub and worker tests never need a real GPU.

docs.title: Engine entry-point discovery
docs.text:
Engines register themselves in their pyproject.toml using the resona.engines entry-point group:

[project.entry-points."resona.engines"]
faster-whisper = "resona_engine_faster_whisper.transcriber:FastWhisperTranscriber"

At startup, resona_asr_core/registry.py scans all installed packages for this group. The RESONA_ENGINE environment variable selects which entry to load (default: faster-whisper). get_transcriber() returns a thread-safe singleton for the lifetime of the process.

Available built-in engines:

Name Package Backend faster-whisper resona-engine-faster-whisper CTranslate2 (default) whisper resona-engine-whisper OpenAI Whisper / PyTorch voxtral resona-engine-voxtral HuggingFace Transformers

Each engine's [project.scripts] entry points to the same resona_engine_server.run:main entrypoint — the same FastAPI application, with a different engine loaded.

docs.title: POST /transcribe
docs.text:
The synchronous transcription endpoint. All parameters come from the multipart form body; none are read from a database.

Request (multipart/form-data):

Field Type Required Description audio_file file Yes Audio file (any format ffmpeg can decode) language string No BCP-47 language tag (e.g. de, en) task string No transcribe (default) or translate initial_prompt string No Hint text to bias the model vad_filter bool No Enable voice-activity filtering word_timestamps bool No Include per-word timestamps in segments

Response (application/json):

{
  "text": "Der Patient klagt über Kopfschmerzen.",
  "language": "de",
  "segments": [
    {
      "start": 0.0,
      "end": 2.4,
      "text": "Der Patient klagt über Kopfschmerzen."
    }
  ]
}

The text field is always the raw transcript. No replacements have been applied.

docs.title: WebSocket endpoints
docs.text: The engine also exposes two WebSocket endpoints for streaming scenarios.

docs.title: WS /ws/transcribe — windowed streaming
docs.text:
Audio is accumulated in an AudioBuffer (2-second windows with 0.5-second overlap). Useful when the client streams audio in real time and wants incremental results.

Client → Server:

{"type": "audio", "data": "<base64 PCM>", "sample_rate": 16000}
{"type": "stop"}

Server → Client:

{"type": "transcript", "text": "...", "is_final": false}
{"type": "transcript", "text": "...", "is_final": true}

docs.title: WS /ws/live — VAD-based live transcription
docs.text:
Audio is segmented by a voice-activity detector (webrtcvad). Each detected speech segment is transcribed independently via LiveTranscriber from resona-asr-core. Suitable for the resona live TUI.

Client → Server:

{"type": "audio_data", "data": "<base64 PCM>"}
{"type": "config", "language": "de", "task": "transcribe"}
{"type": "end_stream"}

Server → Client:

{"type": "interim", "text": "...", "is_final": false}
{"type": "transcript", "text": "...", "is_final": true, "segment_id": 1}
{"type": "stream_ended"}

docs.title: How to add a new engine
docs.text:
See Adding an Engine for the full step-by-step guide. In brief:

  1. Create packages/engine-<name>/ with src-layout.
  2. Implement __init__(self, device: str, modelname: str | None = None) and transcribe(audio: np.ndarray, **kwargs) -> TranscriptionResult.
  3. Register the entry point in pyproject.toml under [project.entry-points."resona.engines"].
  4. Point [project.scripts] at resona_engine_server.run:main.
  5. The engine must not touch the database — apply the request-body test before adding any parameter.

docs.title: Job Lifecycle
docs.text: This page traces what happens to a file from submission until the result is available. There are two paths: the hub path (resona-api plus pull workers) and the local path (CLI only, used only when no hub is configured).

docs.title: Hub path
docs.text:
Client → POST /v1/uploads (multipart file)            → {upload_id, sha256, size}
Client → POST /v1/jobs (Idempotency-Key; {kind, upload_id, ...})
  resona-api:
    derives the organization from the bearer token
    resolves settings, execution profile and postprocess profile revision
    checks policy before admission (private=true by default)
    stores an immutable execution_snapshot; returns 202 {job_id, status: "pending"}

resona-worker (outbound only, long-polls POST /v1/workers/claim):
  hub claims the oldest eligible pending job, mints a 120 s lease
  worker downloads input (GET /v1/workers/jobs/{id}/input, X-Resona-Lease)
  runs the engine in an isolated subprocess, heartbeats every 30 s
  asks /policy right before any external stage
  uploads JobResult (POST /v1/workers/jobs/{id}/result)

Client → GET /v1/jobs/{id}          → JobView {status: "completed", result_available: true}
Client → GET /v1/jobs/{id}/result   → {raw_text, markdown, segments, pages, provenance, ...}

docs.title: Job states
docs.text:
pending → processing → completed | failed | cancelled
State Meaning pending Waiting for a capable worker; queue_reason says why: waiting_capacity (an eligible worker is online and busy), release_not_approved (a worker offers one of the job's tuples, but its release has no promoted evaluation for the job's execution profile and platform), worker_outdated (such a worker's release is approved but does not know an option the job sets, e.g. a 0.1.0 worker and remove_repeated_headers) or no_capable_worker (no online worker of the job's privacy class offers one, e.g. the only CUDA worker runs without a usable GPU, or a diarize job and no such worker reports a verified diarizer) processing Claimed by a worker under a lease completed Result accepted and stored failed Terminal error, attempts_exhausted (3 assignments) or deadline_exceeded (24 h) cancelled Cancelled by the client; the lease is fenced and later worker output is rejected

If a lease expires (worker offline or asleep), the job returns to pending and another worker can claim it. A late result from the old lease gets 409 stale_lease. Execution is at-least-once; the hub accepts one result.

Private jobs go only to workers that an admin approved with resona-admin worker approve --private; cloud opt-in jobs (private: false) go only to workers approved with --non-private, so a private execution environment never receives cloud work. A worker cannot change its approval through its heartbeat, and an OOM failure withdraws a tuple only on that worker, never its hub approval. A job whose endpoint is assigned to one worker (its secret file lives there) is claimed only by that worker. If no capable worker is online, the job waits; the hub never weakens privacy or swaps the model.

DELETE /v1/jobs/{id} in any state removes the job and its files at once; for a processing job it first fences the lease, so the worker's next call gets 409 stale_lease and its output is rejected.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
Content is stored as files under /data/organizations/<storage_id>/jobs/<job_id>/, not in the database. A maintenance loop on the hub applies retention:

  • input: deleted when the job reaches a terminal state
  • result: deleted 24 hours after completion (GET .../result then returns 410)
  • job metadata: deleted after 7 days
  • unattached uploads: deleted after 1 hour

Testbench items are the exception: the original and the run results are stored under <storage_id>/testbench/ and are not touched by these sweeps. A collector copies each testbench job's result into its run file before the 24 h result retention, so the job row and result may expire while the run keeps its data. Testbench jobs have purpose=testbench and need no promoted release tuple.

docs.title: Local path
docs.text:
Only with an explicit --local does the CLI process on this machine; it is never chosen automatically. Without --local, hub errors (unreachable, timeout, failed job) are reported and never fall back to a local or cloud engine; a policy denial exits with code 2.

resona transcribe ./audio/ --local --execution-profile cpu-private

  Settings:
    cached revision from `resona settings pull` for this hub + credential (marked stale: true)
    or built-in private defaults

  For each audio file:
    resolve the execution profile's approved candidates (as hub admission does)
    check_policy on every stage  → policy_denied exits 2
    run the candidate in the worker's execution subprocess (resona_worker.execute)
      with offline model caches and no credentials
    postprocess (profile name, file or inline JSON; LLM stages policy-checked again)

  writes <stem>.md + <stem>.result.json  (or --output-dir; --force to overwrite)

No server, no database

In local mode there is no SQLite database and no job queue. The CLI processes files sequentially and writes the same outputs as hub jobs.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: Resona is a modular transcription platform composed of loosely coupled packages. Each package has a single clear responsibility. Cross-service communication is over HTTP; the engine never sees the database, and the database never runs inference.

docs.title: resona-cli (apps/resona-cli)
docs.text: The user-facing entry point. Provides subcommands for hub jobs (transcribe, doc, watch, jobs), organization settings (settings), recording TUIs (rec, ui), live transcription (live), speech synthesis (speech), and management of hub entries and profiles. Delegates all hub operations to resona-client. Only with an explicit --local does it run a job on this machine, through resona-worker's execution subprocess; it never falls back to local processing automatically.

docs.title: resona-client
docs.text: A thin httpx-based client for the hub's /v1/uploads and /v1/jobs routes, with no ML dependencies. The CLI imports this for all HTTP work. Configuration is read from RESONA_API_URL / RESONA_API_KEY (the org-bound bearer token) or the resona-api entry in ~/.resona/config.json.

docs.title: resona-api (:7000)
docs.text: The hub. Authenticates org-bound bearer tokens issued by resona-admin, accepts uploads (POST /v1/uploads, 200 MiB cap), persists organization-scoped jobs to SQLite (/v1/jobs), leases them to pull workers (/v1/workers/*) and applies retention. It runs no inference for queued jobs. Also exposes an OpenAI-compatible audio API (GET /v1/engines, POST /v1/audio/speech, and POST /v1/audio/transcriptions, an adapter that creates a job and waits for a worker).

docs.title: resona-worker
docs.text: An outbound-only pull worker for a Mac or Linux GPU machine. resona-worker prepare --profile <name> verifies cached weights, runs synthetic jobs and writes a capabilities manifest of tested tuples. resona-worker run --hub <url> --token-file <path> --capabilities-file <manifest> --work-dir <dir> long-polls the hub for jobs, runs each job in an isolated engine subprocess, uploads the result and deletes its scratch data. It offers only tuples that it tested and that the hub approved. It opens no listening port. The worker token comes from resona-admin worker enroll; an admin must approve the worker (resona-admin worker approve) before it can claim jobs. On macOS, resona-worker install runs the worker as a launchd user agent (see Mac Worker).

docs.title: resona-engine-server + engine plugin (:7001)
docs.text: A stateless FastAPI application that loads exactly one engine plugin at startup (selected by RESONA_ENGINE). Accepts audio, runs inference, returns raw {text, language, segments}. No database. No postprocessing. See Stateless Engine Contract for the full design rationale.

docs.title: resona-asr-core
docs.text: The shared vocabulary: Transcriber Protocol, TranscriptionResult TypedDict, the entry-point registry (registry.py), audio loading utilities (audio.py), and the VAD-based live transcriber (live_transcriber.py). Both the engine server and the CLI's InProcessEngine depend on this package.

docs.title: resona-postprocess
docs.text: A composable str → str pipeline: regex replacement steps and LLM steps (via litellm). Runs inside resona-worker for hub jobs and in the CLI process in local mode; every stage is checked against the job's ExecutionPolicy first. See Postprocessing Pipeline.

docs.title: resona-cloud-stt / resona-cloud-tts
docs.text: Provider adapters for cloud speech services. No persistent state; each call is self-contained. Activated automatically when the corresponding API key environment variable is present.

docs.title: Cross-package import rules
docs.text:
Only the following direct cross-package imports are permitted. All other cross-service communication must go over HTTP.

resona-cli  →  resona_asr_core.live_transcriber   (live command; base dependency)
resona-cli  →  resona_asr_core.registry           (InProcessEngine; base dependency)
resona-cli  →  resona_client.client               (all HTTP operations)

Never import across service boundaries

resona-cli and resona-client must never import from resona-api or resona-engine-server. resona-engine-server must never import from resona-api. Import the package over HTTP, not as a Python module.

docs.title: Data storage layout
docs.text:
All server-side data lives under DATA_PATH (default ./data):

DATA_PATH/
├── db/                                   ← SQLite database (jobs, organizations, credentials, settings)
└── organizations/<storage_id>/jobs/<id>/ ← job input and result files (expire per retention)

DATA_PATH, FILE_PATH and DB_PATH are resolved in resona_api/paths.py and read via python-decouple so they can be overridden by environment variables or a .env file. Content lives in expiring files, not in the database: inputs are deleted on terminal state, results after 24 hours, metadata after 7 days.

docs.title: Postprocessing Pipeline
docs.text: Postprocessing is the layer between raw engine output and the final stored transcript. The engine returns exactly what the model produced; everything else — text normalisation, dictation-command expansion, LLM reformatting, structured data extraction — is the pipeline's responsibility.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
A profile is a JSON file (or inline JSON string) that groups three things:

  1. An initial_prompt list — phrases passed to the ASR engine to bias vocabulary.
  2. An ordered list of steps — the postprocessing pipeline.
  3. Metadata: name and description.
{
  "name": "my-profile",
  "description": "German medical dictation with LLM formatting",
  "initial_prompt": ["Befund", "Diagnose", "Medikation"],
  "steps": [
    {
      "type": "replacements",
      "rules": [
        {"pattern": "\\bKomma\\b", "replacement": ","},
        {"pattern": "\\bPunkt\\b",  "replacement": "."},
        {"pattern": "\\bAbsatz\\b", "replacement": "\n"}
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "llm",
      "name": "format",
      "prompt": "Format this medical dictation as a structured clinical note.",
      "model": "ollama/llama3"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: replacements
docs.text:
Applies a list of regex replacement rules in order. Rules are case-insensitive by default. Each rule has pattern and replacement keys; the replacement may reference capture groups.

Supply either: - rules — inline array of rule objects - source — path to a JSON file containing the rules array (relative to the profile's directory or ~/.resona/profiles/)

{"type": "replacements", "rules": [{"pattern": "\\bKomma\\b", "replacement": ","}]}

The standalone apply_replacements(text, rules) function is available for use outside a full pipeline.

docs.title: llm
docs.text:
Sends the current text to a language model using litellm. The model's response replaces the text. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint is supported.

{
  "type": "llm",
  "name": "format",
  "prompt": "Format this as a structured medical report.",
  "model": "ollama/llama3",
  "api_base": "http://localhost:11434"
}

Fields:

Field Required Description type yes "llm" name no Label for this step (used in logs) prompt yes System prompt sent to the model endpoint no Id of an entry in the execution policy registry. Preferred form; hub profiles must use it model no Explicit local CLI mode only (legacy step). Falls back to RESONA_LLM_MODEL; no default model exists api_base no Explicit local CLI mode only (legacy step). Overrides RESONA_LLM_API_BASE temperature no Sampling temperature max_tokens no Maximum tokens to generate timeout no Seconds per model call (default 120) chunk_chars no Chunked mode (integer ≥ 1000): the text is sent in chunks of about this many characters, see below max_attempts no Chunked mode only: calls per chunk before the step fails (1–10, default 3) max_length_deviation no Chunked mode only: reject a chunk reply whose length differs from the chunk by more than this fraction (e.g. 0.3) preserve_markup no Chunked mode only: reject a chunk reply that changes HTML comments/placeholders, heading levels or the cell count of any table row

docs.title: Chunked mode (long Markdown)
docs.text:
A step with chunk_chars splits the Markdown with chunking.split_markdown: a chunk ends at the furthest blank-line (block) boundary that keeps it within chunk_chars; only a single block longer than that is cut at a line boundary. A pipe table or a fenced code block is never cut, even when it alone is longer than chunk_chars. The chunks concatenate to the input exactly; each chunk is sent without its surrounding whitespace, which is restored around the reply.

  • A chunk call that fails is retried up to max_attempts calls in total. When a chunk still fails, the step raises PostprocessStepFailed. run() re-raises it like PolicyDenied, so the job fails (postprocess_failed, retryable) instead of silently skipping the polish.
  • A reply that fails max_length_deviation or preserve_markup is not retried: the raw chunk is kept and the result gets the warning polish_chunk_rejected:<chunk number>:<length|markup>.
  • A leading <think>…</think> block and a code fence wrapped around the whole reply are removed before the checks.

Without chunk_chars an llm step keeps its single-call behaviour: a failure is logged and the step is skipped (postprocess_step_skipped:<name>).

docs.title: extract
docs.text:
Sends the current text to a language model and returns structured JSON data. The text is not modified; instead the extracted data is stored alongside the transcript (in job.structured server-side).

{
  "type": "extract",
  "name": "icd_codes",
  "prompt": "Return a JSON object {\"codes\": [...]} listing all ICD-10 codes mentioned.",
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini"
}

temperature, max_tokens and timeout apply as for llm; the call is made in JSON mode.

docs.title: PostprocessResult
docs.text:
build_pipeline(profile, policy=policy).run(text) returns a PostprocessResult:

@dataclass
class PostprocessResult:
    text: str             # final postprocessed text (all llm/replacements steps applied)
    data: dict            # accumulated output from all extract steps, keyed by step name
    warnings: list[str]   # content-free warnings, e.g. polish_chunk_rejected:<n>:<reason>

A text step may return a StepOutput(text, warnings) instead of a string; chunked llm steps do.

docs.title: The bundled default profile
docs.text:
resona-postprocess ships a profiles/default.json (rules in default_replacements.json) that turns German dictation commands into Markdown. It is used automatically when no profile is specified.

Spoken Written Komma , Punkt . Doppelpunkt : Ausrufezeichen ! Fragezeichen ? Absatz blank line (Markdown paragraph) Anstrich - (list item) Kapitel Titel ## Titel Klammer auf / zu, Eckige Klammer auf / zu ( ) [ ]

Every command pattern has word boundaries ( ); rules run case-insensitively, so without them Zeitpunkt became Zeit.. Order matters: the four medical heading rules (Kapitel Verlauf|Medikation|Psychopathologischer Befund|Pro[cz]edere, no terminator needed, an immediately spoken Absatz/Punkt/Doppelpunkt/Komma is swallowed) run first, then the general Kapitel rule, then brackets, then Doppelpunkt before Punkt, then Absatz. Three cleanup rules close the list: trailing spaces before a newline, runs of 3+ newlines → one blank line, leading/trailing whitespace of the whole text removed. Name corrections (Monique → Monic, …) come first and are part of default only.

The general Kapitel rule fires only for a title of one to five words (characters other than whitespace and .,;:!?()[]; a . or , between digits is allowed, so F32.1 stays whole; command words like Komma are excluded) followed by an optional comma and a terminator: Absatz, Punkt, Doppelpunkt, Fragezeichen, Ausrufezeichen, !, ?, :, or a . with no digit on either side (3. Mai is no terminator). Negative lookbehinds skip Kapitel after articles, prepositions and ordinals (im, das, dem, vom, zum, letzten, …), so prose such as wie im Kapitel zuvor beschrieben. is untouched. Without a match the text stays as spoken. The punctuation commands absorb one adjacent punctuation mark on each side (, Komma, → ,, . Punkt. → .), so Whisper's own punctuation is not doubled. Rules that consume leading whitespace use (?<![ ])[ ]* instead of \s*: they never cross a newline (only Absatz and the heading rules produce line breaks) and stay linear on long space runs. Whole-word commands still hit ordinary words (der wichtigste Punkt, im dritten Absatz); rules cannot avoid that.

This is a behaviour change for every organization using the bundled default (see the guide's "Behaviour change" note, which also shows how to keep the v0.1.0 rules as a stored profile). The bundled profile reaches workers as source: default_replacements.json and is resolved from each worker's installed resona-postprocess, so the snapshot hash does not cover the rule content and a mixed-release fleet can give different output for the same snapshot.

docs.title: The bundled transcript profiles
docs.text:
profiles/transcript-markdown-de.json (transcript-markdown-de) is one replacements step with the dictation command rules of default_replacements.json (without the name corrections), inline because hosted profiles reject source; a test keeps them equal to the tail of default_replacements.json. No LLM, runs on any worker.

profiles/transcript-polish-de.json (transcript-polish-de) runs the same rules, then a chunked llm step on endpoint local-llm. Its German prompt allows only changes to capitalization (sentence starts, after headings, list items, nouns), punctuation and whitespace; it forbids changing, adding or removing any word, even one that looks misrecognized, and names numbers, units, doses, drug names, diagnoses, codes and proper names as untouchable. Settings: chunk_chars 12000, max_attempts 3, max_length_deviation 0.1, preserve_markup true, temperature 0, max_tokens 8192, timeout 600. preserve_markup (markup_signature) compares only HTML comments, the heading-level sequence, per-row table cell counts and the ordered speaker labels of a diarized transcript (**Sprecher N:** at a line start); merged paragraphs, joined list items, changed heading text or a changed word or number pass it and are only bounded by the length guard. The endpoint registration is the same as for document-polish-de below.

docs.title: The bundled document polish profile
docs.text: profiles/document-polish-de.json (document-polish-de) is a single chunked llm step for Docling Markdown of German documents. Its German prompt allows only OCR fixes: hyphenation across line breaks, misrecognized umlauts/ß, confused or stray characters, merged/split words. It forbids adding, removing, summarizing or rephrasing content and requires headings, tables, page markers and the <!-- image --> / <!-- formula-not-decoded --> placeholders to stay verbatim. Settings: endpoint local-llm, chunk_chars 12000, max_attempts 3, max_length_deviation 0.3, preserve_markup true, temperature 0, max_tokens 8192, timeout 600. The endpoint id names no host: an org admin registers a local_llm endpoint with the id local-llm and a loopback url on the approved worker. It is not resolved by name from the package: upload it to the hub as an organization profile (see Linux Worker).

docs.title: Profile resolution
docs.text: resolve_profile(ref, profiles_dir) accepts any of: - A Profile object — returned as-is - A dict — parsed as a profile - A string starting with { — parsed as inline JSON - A string ending with .json that exists on disk — loaded from that path - A plain name string — looked up as <profiles_dir>/<name>.json; falls back to the bundled default profile when name == "default"

docs.title: Hub mode (resona-worker)
docs.text:
engine returns {text, language, segments}
    ↓
worker takes the postprocess profile revision from the job's execution_snapshot
    ↓
build_pipeline(profile, policy=<job ExecutionPolicy>) checks every stage first
    ↓
result = pipeline.run(text)   (PolicyDenied is raised, never swallowed)
    ↓
raw_text stays the engine's text; the engine's Markdown moves to raw_markdown when a step changed it; markdown is the polished text
    ↓
worker uploads the result; the hub marks the job completed

Before each llm/extract step the worker asks the hub for a fresh policy decision on that endpoint. After the job's last step on an endpoint that has an unload_url, the worker POSTs to that URL (best effort, 10 s timeout) so the model server frees the GPU for the next job. A 2xx answer is logged at info level; another status or a transport error is a warning naming the endpoint id and the status code or exception type, never content.

The engine receives profile.initial_prompt_string() as its initial_prompt. It never receives replacement rules — postprocessing is the worker's responsibility, not the engine's.

docs.title: Local mode (CLI process)
docs.text:
engine returns {text, language, segments}
    ↓
CLI resolves profile (--profile flag or config.json default_profile or bundled "default")
    ↓
result = build_pipeline(profile).run(text)
    ↓
writes <input>.txt  (or --output-dir/<name>.txt)

Postprocessing never runs inside the engine

The engine is unaware of profiles, replacements, or LLM steps. This is enforced by the Stateless Engine Contract.

docs.title: Config Files
docs.text:
Resona reads optional config files from ~/.resona/. None are required — sensible defaults apply when they are absent.

~/.resona/
├── config.json          # hub entries, auto-start settings, default_engine, default_profile
├── settings-cache/      # non-secret cached organization settings (resona settings pull)
└── profiles/            # postprocessing profiles (JSON files)
    ├── default.json     # optional: override the bundled default profile
    └── my-profile.json  # any named profile

docs.title: config.json
docs.text: Lists the hubs (resona-api servers) the resona CLI can use, plus the default local engine for resona live and the default profile.

docs.title: Annotated example
docs.text:
{
  "default_engine": "auto",
  "default_profile": "medical-de",
  "engines": [
    {
      "name": "gpu-server",
      "api_url": "http://gpu-machine:7000",
      "api_key": "",
      "ssh_host": "user@server.example.com",
      "ssh_remote_port": 7000
    },
    {
      "name": "local",
      "api_url": "http://localhost:7000",
      "compose_dir": "~/resona"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Top-level fields
docs.text: Field Type Default Description default_engine string "auto" Local in-process engine for resona live; auto picks the platform default default_profile string — Default postprocessing profile name engines array [] Priority-ordered list of hub entries

docs.title: Hub entry fields
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description name string yes Identifier of the entry api_url string yes Base URL of the resona-api server api_key string no API key for the server compose_dir string no Docker Compose project directory; enables auto-start ssh_host string no SSH tunnel target, "[user@]hostname[:port]". The CLI opens the tunnel before connecting. ssh_remote_port integer no Remote port on the SSH host (defaults to the port in api_url)

Entries describe hubs only; legacy cloud provider entries are dropped with a warning on load. Processing is private by default, and cloud processing is controlled by the organization setting cloud_enabled plus --allow-cloud, never by local config or provider API keys.

docs.title: settings-cache/
docs.text: resona settings get and resona settings pull cache the organization's revisioned settings per hub URL and organization_id in ~/.resona/settings-cache/<hash>.json (hub_url, organization_id, credential — a SHA-256 prefix of the token, never the token —, revision, etag, settings, fetched_at, stale). --local runs use this cache and set stale: true.

docs.title: profiles/
docs.text:
The ~/.resona/profiles/ directory holds postprocessing profile JSON files for --local runs. Each file is named <profile-name>.json.

To add a profile:

mkdir -p ~/.resona/profiles/
cp my-profile.json ~/.resona/profiles/
resona transcribe dictation.mp3 --local --profile my-profile

Hub jobs use profiles stored server-side in RESONA_PROFILES_DIR, managed with resona profiles push/pull/list/show/delete. The CLI passes only the stored profile name to the hub; file paths and inline JSON are accepted only with --local.

See Postprocessing Profiles for the profile file format and a full example.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
All configuration is read with python-decouple: environment variables take precedence over values in a .env file. Copy .env.example to .env to get started.

Exception: resona-client

resona-client uses os.getenv() for RESONA_API_URL and RESONA_API_KEY (the org-bound bearer token) because it has no python-decouple dependency. All other packages use config() from python-decouple.

docs.title: resona-engine-server (:7001)
docs.text: Variable Default Description RESONA_ENGINE faster-whisper Engine to load per engine-server process: faster-whisper, whisper, or voxtral RESONA_ENGINE_KEY (unset) Optional API key for the engine; auth is disabled when not set LOGLEVEL info Log level: debug, info, warning, error

docs.title: resona-api (:7000)
docs.text: Variable Default Description RESONA_ENGINE_URLS http://localhost:7001 Comma-separated list of engine-server URLs; the API probes all and load-balances across reachable ones RESONA_DEFAULT_ENGINE (first available) Engine name to use for requests that do not specify one RESONA_ENGINE_KEY (unset) Not used by resona-api: the hub sends no key to engine-servers (the bridged /ws/live takes none). Keep engine-servers on a private network instead RESONA_BOOTSTRAP_ORGANIZATION_ID (unset) Organization that owns jobs already in an upgraded database. Required only when a pre-identity database with job rows is first migrated; startup refuses without it. Hub access uses org-scoped credentials issued by resona-admin, not a shared key DATA_PATH ./data Root directory for all persistent data (SQLite DB and expiring per-organization job files) RESONA_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES 209715200 (200 MiB) Maximum size of one upload or worker result; enforced while streaming, larger requests get 413 RESONA_MAX_TEXT_UPLOAD_BYTES 2097152 (2 MiB) Maximum size of one UTF-8 text upload (text jobs, postprocess only); larger text gets 413 RESONA_PROFILES_DIR <DATA_PATH>/profiles Directory where the bundled and file-backed profile sources are resolved for CLI and postprocessing; hosted profile revisions are stored in the database per organization and served by GET /profiles RESONA_SYNC_WAIT_SECONDS 60 Seconds POST /v1/audio/transcriptions waits for a worker to finish the job; on timeout it answers 504 with the job_id while the job keeps running LOGLEVEL info Log level: debug, info, warning, error

docs.title: resona-client / resona CLI
docs.text: Variable Default Description RESONA_API_URL http://localhost:7000 resona-api base URL RESONA_API_KEY (unset) Org-bound token issued by resona-admin credential issue; sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>

docs.title: resona-postprocess / resona-cli (local mode)
docs.text: Variable Default Description RESONA_LLM_MODEL (unset) Explicit local CLI mode only: model for llm/extract steps that set no model. There is no default model; the hub never reads this variable RESONA_LLM_API_BASE (unset) Explicit local CLI mode only: API base for legacy LLM steps (for example a local Ollama instance). A non-loopback base makes the step cloud, which private runs deny RESONA_PROFILES_DIR ~/.resona/profiles/ Directory where the CLI looks for named profile files in --local runs

docs.title: Cloud provider keys
docs.text:
Provider API keys are read from environment variables and are never stored in ~/.resona/config.json. A key never enables cloud processing by itself: cloud stages also need the organization setting cloud_enabled=true, a job submitted with --allow-cloud, and a hub-approved non-private worker. The CLI never calls a provider directly.

Variable Provider Used for DEEPGRAM_API_KEY Deepgram Deepgram STT (nova-3) + TTS ELEVENLABS_API_KEY ElevenLabs ElevenLabs STT (scribe_v1) + TTS OPENAI_API_KEY OpenAI OpenAI Whisper API (whisper-1) + TTS (tts-1)

docs.title: Model names
docs.text:
Override the default model loaded by each local engine:

Variable Default Engine DEFAULT_FASTWHISPER_MODEL large-v3 resona-engine-faster-whisper (CTranslate2) DEFAULT_WHISPER_MODEL large-v3 resona-engine-whisper (PyTorch) DEFAULT_VOXTRAL_MODEL openai/whisper-large-v3 resona-engine-voxtral (HuggingFace Transformers)

docs.title: Docker and .env file
docs.text:
When using docker compose -f docker-compose.resona.yml, variables are loaded from the .env file in the project root via the env_file directive on the API service. Engine containers have their key variables hard-coded in docker-compose.resona.yml and can be overridden by adding them to .env.

cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env, then:
docker compose -f docker-compose.resona.yml --profile faster-whisper up -d

Credentials

Hub access uses org-scoped credentials. Issue one on the hub host with resona-admin credential issue --organization <id> --role client, then send Authorization: Bearer <token> with every request (REST also accepts the same token in X-API-Key). Tokens are shown once; the hub stores only their SHA-256 hash. There is no auth-disabled mode.

Custom LLM endpoint

To run postprocessing on a local Ollama instance in local CLI mode, set: 

RESONA_LLM_MODEL=ollama/llama3
RESONA_LLM_API_BASE=http://localhost:11434
The loopback endpoint keeps the step private. Any model supported by litellm works, but cloud models are denied unless the run allows cloud (--allow-cloud with cloud_enabled=true).

docs.title: /admin - hub management console
docs.text: Scope: the static /admin page (index.html, admin.js, admin.css). Mode: Operate. Audience: the hub operator (mostly), occasionally org admins; desktop short sessions and phone quick checks. Task: see hub state (workers online/approved, tokens, job queue, settings, baselines, testbench) and act (approve, revoke, issue, cancel, delete, create org). Product facts: admin-product.md.

docs.title: Direction
docs.text: IBM Carbon played straight, for data-dense reading: a g100 shell, a g10 page, Carbon data tables for every list, Carbon tokens and spacing only. No custom palette, no decorative motifs. State comes before action: every row shows what is true (online, approved, revoked, queued) as a tag before any menu offers an action.

docs.title: Shell
docs.text:
• cds-header in the g100 zone: menu button (cds-header-menu-button, rail mode), product name "Resona hub", then global actions: the selected organization (mono), an organization switcher (operators only) whose cds-header-panel lists every organization plus "Create organization", the signed-in role (account panel with credential and organization), and Sign out.
  • cds-side-nav with icon links: Overview, Workers, Credentials, Jobs, Settings, Baselines, Testbench. At 66rem and wider it is a 3rem rail beside the page; below that it is hidden until the menu button expands it, and choosing a section closes it.
  • Hash routing: #/overview, #/workers, #/credentials, #/jobs, #/settings, #/baselines, #/testbench. Reload and the back button keep the section; an unknown or empty hash shows Overview.
  • Sign-in: a g100 bar and one tile with a cds-password-input for the token and a Sign in button. A 401 clears the stored token and says "Token invalid or revoked"; a 403 from /v1/admin/me says the token is not an organization admin or hub operator token.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
Each section has a page header (organization label, title, one-sentence note, page tools such as Refresh) and its tables.

  • Overview: a row of clickable tiles linking to their section (workers online with approved / not revoked counts, live credentials, pending jobs with the oldest wait, settings revision) and a "Needs attention" table derived only from loaded data: workers reporting capabilities without approval, approved workers that are offline, pending jobs with a queue reason, approved capabilities a worker no longer reports.
  • Workers: name, ID, status (online/offline/revoked), last seen, approval, capability summary, runtime. The expanded row holds the facts and the capability list. Row menu: approve private, approve non-private, revoke.
  • Credentials: credential ID, role, state, worker, issued. Toolbar actions issue a client or an org-admin token. Row menu: revoke; disabled with the reason for the caller's own credential and for worker credentials (revoked through their worker).
  • Jobs: job, kind, status, waiting (duration and queue reason for pending jobs), execution profile, privacy, result availability, created. The expanded row holds the timeline, attempt, candidate, error and result facts. Cursor paging with "Load more" via next_cursor. Row menu (org admins in their own organization only): cancel, delete. Operators see metadata without a menu column.
  • Settings: read-only. Revision tag, a structured list of the top-level keys with short values, and the full JSON in a multi-line cds-code-snippet with copy.
  • Baselines: baselines table (execution profile, platform, revision, release, shortened corpus digest, created; full digest in the expanded row) and approved releases table.
  • Testbench: org admins in their own organization only (operators see why it is closed). Status strip with enable/disable (GET /v1/settings ETag, PUT with If-Match), then a cds-tabs switch: Items (kind/status filters, items table, Contribute modal with cds-file-uploader), Runs (the open item: original preview from a blob URL for audio and PNG, download, reference cds-textarea with save, candidate checkboxes with worker counts, runs table, word diff), Leaderboard (audio and document tables, best value per column marked).

docs.title: Table pattern
docs.text:
Every list goes through one dataTable(cfg) helper in admin.js:

  • cds-table size md (sm for dense testbench tables) with title and description, a toolbar with cds-table-toolbar-search (filters the loaded rows client-side, including expanded-row text), a refresh button and the section's primary action.
  • Sortable headers where the column has a meaningful order; sorting and filtering act on the loaded row array, so a re-render keeps them.
  • Secondary detail lives in cds-table-expanded-row; expanded state survives a refresh.
  • Loading shows cds-table-skeleton; an empty table shows one sentence that says what makes a row appear (for example: enroll a worker with resona-admin worker enroll).
  • Status is a cds-tag: green online/approved/completed/live, gray offline, red revoked/failed, purple pending/queued, blue processing, warm-gray cancelled. Capabilities: green approved and reported, cool-gray reported but not approved, magenta approved but no longer reported; each tag carries a screen-reader text equivalent and a legend explains the colours.

docs.title: Row actions and modals
docs.text:
• One cds-overflow-menu per row instead of rows of buttons. Destructive items are danger; an action that is not allowed stays visible, disabled, with the reason in its label.
  • Destructive actions confirm in a cds-modal with a danger primary button; the title names the object ("Revoke credential cred_…?"), the body states the consequence, the secondary button goes back.
  • Issued token: a cds-modal that does not close on an outside click, with a warning inline notification "Shown once", the credential ID and the token in a cds-code-snippet type=single with copy. "Done" removes the token from the DOM and from memory. The token is never re-displayed or logged.
  • Create organization and Contribute are small form modals.

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text: Success and info: cds-toast-notification in the top-right stack. Errors: the page-level cds-inline-notification banner keeps the API code and message from the {error, message} body (fallbacks: detail.message, a validation detail list, the HTTP status text). Sign-in errors stay on the sign-in tile.

docs.title: Tokens and type
docs.text:
• Theme: g10 on :root (page), g100 zone class on the header and sign-in bar, cds--layer-two on panels that sit on a layer.
  • Colours, spacing and type only through Carbon custom properties (var(--cds-…)), and only theme-level tokens: component tokens such as --cds-tag-background-* are not defined on :root. Word diff: missing words --cds-text-error with line-through, added words on --cds-highlight with a --cds-support-success underline (never colour alone).
  • IBM Plex Sans for text; IBM Plex Mono (.mono) for every machine identifier: IDs, digests, revisions, model and candidate names, execution profiles. Numbers use tabular figures.
  • admin.css stays small: layout, phone rules and the few things Carbon does not cover.

docs.title: Phone (under 42rem)
docs.text:
• Header shows the menu button, the organization (and the switcher for operators), account and sign out; the side nav opens from the menu button.
  • No page-level horizontal scroll. Tables may scroll inside their own container; columns marked secondary are hidden and their values stay in the expanded row, which is pinned to the viewport width. Toolbar actions wrap onto their own line.
  • Overview tiles stack in one column.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• CSP: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; media-src blob:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'. No inline scripts, no style="…" or on* attributes in HTML, no external URLs. Setting element.style from JS is allowed.
  • No innerHTML/outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML: the DOM is built with createElement/textContent; icons are Carbon icon descriptors rendered with createElementNS.
  • admin.js is an ES module (<script type="module" src="/admin/admin.js">) that imports icon descriptors from /admin/vendor/carbon/carbon.js; importing that bundle registers the cds-* elements. Component methods are called only after customElements.whenDefined (and updateComplete where the shadow DOM is needed).
  • index.html loads /admin/vendor/carbon/carbon.css, then /admin/admin.css.
  • The Carbon bundle is vendored prebuilt in static/admin/vendor/carbon/ (script, theme CSS, Plex fonts, gzip twins). To add a component or icon, edit packages/api/admin-vendor/src/entry.js and run packages/api/admin-vendor/build.sh (bun); see packages/api/admin-vendor/README.md.
  • Operator scope never includes job content: the testbench and job cancel/delete are closed to the hub operator role.

docs.title: Platform
docs.text: web

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
• Hub operator (primary): the owner of the Resona hub (https://resona.ecsplico.de). Uses /admin for occasional checks: is a worker online, issue or revoke a token, look at the job queue, read settings and baselines. Manages every organization.
  • Org admins (rare): manage only their own organization's workers, credentials and jobs.

docs.title: Product Purpose
docs.text: Resona is a private transcription and document-conversion hub: clients submit audio and documents as jobs; approved workers (Mac/Metal, Linux/CUDA, CPU) pull and run them; results return to the organization. /admin is the hub's management console for workers, credentials, jobs, settings and evaluation baselines. Success: the operator sees the hub's state at a glance and acts (approve, revoke, issue) without the CLI.

docs.title: Positioning
docs.text: Privacy-first: jobs carry a privacy class, private jobs run only on approved private workers, and the hub never shows job content, filenames or tokens beyond the one-time issue response. Production models run only after an evaluation baseline is promoted per execution profile and platform.

docs.title: Operating Context
docs.text:
• Desktop browser for short sessions, and phone for quick checks (e.g. whether a worker is online).
  • Sign-in with a bearer token kept in sessionStorage; server-side setup and partial worker approval stay in the resona-admin CLI.

docs.title: Capabilities and Constraints
docs.text:
• Static page served by the hub (packages/api/src/resona_api/static/admin/), no build step, vanilla JS.
  • Strict CSP: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; media-src blob:. No external assets; third-party code is vendored. No innerHTML with API data.
  • Component library: IBM Carbon web components (vendored bundle, g10/g100 themes), chosen for data-dense tables.
  • Terminology: organization, worker (approved / private / revoked, reported vs approved capabilities), credential (client, org_admin, hub_operator, worker), job (kind, status, queue reason, execution profile, candidate), settings revision, baseline (execution profile × platform, revision), approved release.

docs.title: Evidence on Hand
docs.text: Live hub data (org ecsplico: workers lorien-1 and mac-matthias, five baselines). No customer names, metrics or testimonials exist; none may be invented.

docs.title: Product Principles
docs.text:
1. State before action: the console shows what is true (online, approved, revoked) before offering buttons.
  2. Secrets are shown once and never logged or re-displayed.
  3. Destructive actions confirm; foreign or missing IDs are indistinguishable.
  4. Operator scope never includes job content.

docs.title: Adding a New Engine
docs.text: An engine is a Python package that wraps an ASR backend and exposes it through the Transcriber protocol. The same FastAPI server (resona-engine-server) runs for every engine — only the backend class changes.

docs.title: The engine contract
docs.text:
Before writing any code, understand what an engine is and is not responsible for.

The engine MUST The engine must NOT Accept audio: np.ndarray (16 kHz, float32, mono) Access the database Return TranscriptionResult(text, language, segments) Apply replacements or postprocessing Accept language, task, initial_prompt, word_timestamps, vad_filter Delete audio files Be stateless — every call is self-contained Make outbound HTTP calls Implement __init__(self, device: str, modelname: str \| None = None)

Postprocessing is the caller's responsibility (resona-api or the CLI's local pipeline). The engine returns raw ASR output only.

docs.title: Step 1 — Create the package directory
docs.text:
packages/engine-myengine/
└── src/
    └── resona_engine_myengine/
        ├── __init__.py
        └── transcriber.py

Follow the src-layout used by all other engine packages. The module name must be resona_engine_<name> where <name> matches the entry-point key you will register in step 4.

docs.title: Step 2 — Implement the transcriber class
docs.text:
# packages/engine-myengine/src/resona_engine_myengine/transcriber.py

import logging
import numpy as np
from decouple import config

from resona_asr_core.protocol import TranscriptionResult

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

DEFAULT_MODEL: str = config("DEFAULT_MYENGINE_MODEL", default="my-model-v1")


class MyEngineTranscriber:
    """My custom ASR backend."""

    def __init__(self, device: str = "cpu", modelname: str | None = None):
        model_name = modelname or DEFAULT_MODEL
        log.info(f"Loading MyEngine model: {model_name} on {device}")
        # initialise the backend here
        self.model = ...

    def transcribe(
        self,
        audio: np.ndarray,
        *,
        language: str = "de",
        task: str = "transcribe",
        initial_prompt: str | None = None,
        word_timestamps: bool = False,
        vad_filter: bool = False,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> TranscriptionResult:
        # call the backend
        result = self.model.run(audio, language=language, task=task)

        return TranscriptionResult(
            text=result.text,
            language=result.language,
            segments=result.segments,
        )

Key points:

  • Import TranscriptionResult from resona_asr_core.protocol, not defined locally.
  • Read model configuration via config() from python-decouple — never use os.environ[].
  • The constructor signature (self, device, modelname) is fixed — the registry calls it this way.
  • Accept **kwargs in transcribe for forward compatibility.

docs.title: Step 3 — Write pyproject.toml
docs.text:
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "resona-engine-myengine"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "My custom ASR backend for Resona"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = [
    "resona-asr-core",
    "resona-engine-server",
    "my-asr-library>=1.0",
]

[tool.uv.sources]
resona-asr-core = { workspace = true }
resona-engine-server = { workspace = true }

[project.entry-points."resona.engines"]
my-engine = "resona_engine_myengine.transcriber:MyEngineTranscriber"

[project.scripts]
resona-engine-myengine = "resona_engine_server.run:main"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/resona_engine_myengine"]

Critical fields:

  • [project.entry-points."resona.engines"] — the key (my-engine) is the value RESONA_ENGINE must be set to. It is also what appears in resona engines status.
  • [project.scripts] — the script name is the command users run to start this engine. It always points to resona_engine_server.run:main — the shared FastAPI app.
  • [tool.uv.sources] — both workspace deps must be declared here.

docs.title: Step 4 — Register in the workspace
docs.text:
Open the root pyproject.toml and confirm the members glob covers your new package. The current glob packages/* already does — no change needed unless you chose a non-standard directory.

Sync the workspace to install the new package editable:

uv sync --all-packages

Verify the entry point is visible:

python -c "from importlib.metadata import entry_points; print(entry_points(group='resona.engines'))"

You should see my-engine listed alongside the built-in engines.

docs.title: Step 5 — Verify the engine starts
docs.text:
RESONA_ENGINE=my-engine uv run resona-engine-myengine

The server should start on :7001 and /health should return your engine name:

{"status": "ok", "engine": "my-engine", "models": ["my-model-v1"]}

docs.title: Step 6 — Test the engine
docs.text:
Create packages/engine-myengine/tests/test_transcriber.py:

import numpy as np
import pytest
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from resona_asr_core.protocol import TranscriptionResult


def test_transcribe_returns_required_fields():
    """Engine must return text, language, and segments."""
    from resona_engine_myengine.transcriber import MyEngineTranscriber

    # Patch the backend so no model is actually loaded
    with patch("resona_engine_myengine.transcriber.MyBackend") as MockBackend:
        mock_instance = MagicMock()
        mock_instance.run.return_value = MagicMock(
            text="hello world",
            language="de",
            segments=[{"start": 0.0, "end": 1.0, "text": "hello world"}],
        )
        MockBackend.return_value = mock_instance

        t = MyEngineTranscriber(device="cpu")
        audio = np.zeros(16000, dtype=np.float32)
        result = t.transcribe(audio, language="de")

    assert result["text"] == "hello world"
    assert result["language"] == "de"
    assert isinstance(result["segments"], list)


def test_transcribe_no_postprocessing():
    """Engine must return raw text without applying replacements."""
    from resona_engine_myengine.transcriber import MyEngineTranscriber

    with patch("resona_engine_myengine.transcriber.MyBackend") as MockBackend:
        raw_text = "Komma bitte Punkt"
        mock_instance = MagicMock()
        mock_instance.run.return_value = MagicMock(
            text=raw_text, language="de", segments=[]
        )
        MockBackend.return_value = mock_instance

        t = MyEngineTranscriber(device="cpu")
        result = t.transcribe(np.zeros(16000, dtype=np.float32))

    # "Komma" must NOT have been replaced with "," — that is the caller's job
    assert result["text"] == raw_text

Also add an HTTP-level contract test using the shared engine-server fixture pattern (mock resona_engine_server.app.get_transcriber):

import io
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from resona_asr_core.protocol import TranscriptionResult


def test_http_contract():
    mock_t = MagicMock()
    mock_t.transcribe.return_value = TranscriptionResult(
        text="raw transcript", language="de", segments=[]
    )

    with patch("resona_engine_server.app.get_transcriber", return_value=mock_t):
        with patch("resona_engine_server.auth.config", return_value=None):
            from resona_engine_server.app import app
            client = TestClient(app)

    with patch("resona_engine_server.app.load_audio", return_value=__import__("numpy").zeros(16000)):
        resp = client.post(
            "/transcribe",
            files={"audio_file": ("t.wav", io.BytesIO(b"\x00" * 100), "audio/wav")},
        )

    assert resp.status_code == 200
    body = resp.json()
    assert set(body.keys()) == {"text", "language", "segments"}
    assert "md" not in body

Run the tests:

uv run pytest packages/engine-myengine/tests/

docs.title: Step 7 — Register in config.json for CLI use
docs.text:
To make resona transcribe --engine my-engine work without setting environment variables, add a server entry to ~/.resona/config.json:

{
  "entries": [
    {
      "name": "my-engine",
      "type": "resona-api",
      "url": "http://localhost:7000"
    }
  ],
  "default_engine": "my-engine"
}

Then start the engine and API with:

RESONA_ENGINE=my-engine uv run resona-engine-myengine &
uv run resona-api &
uv run resona transcribe ./audio/ --engine my-engine

docs.title: Engine contract checklist
docs.text:
Before opening a pull request, verify every item:

  • [ ] transcribe() signature matches the Transcriber protocol exactly
  • [ ] TranscriptionResult imported from resona_asr_core.protocol
  • [ ] Constructor is __init__(self, device: str, modelname: str | None = None)
  • [ ] Model config read via config() from python-decouple, not os.environ[]
  • [ ] No database imports anywhere in the engine package
  • [ ] No calls to apply_replacements() or any postprocess module
  • [ ] No file deletion anywhere in the engine package
  • [ ] Entry-point key in pyproject.toml matches the intended RESONA_ENGINE value
  • [ ] [project.scripts] points to resona_engine_server.run:main
  • [ ] Tests cover: required fields returned, no postprocessing applied, HTTP contract

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: All tests use pytest. The workspace root pyproject.toml configures --import-mode=importlib so packages do not need to be installed in development mode for tests to find them (though they are, because of uv sync --all-packages).

docs.title: Running tests
docs.text:
# All packages at once
uv run pytest

# Single package
uv run pytest packages/engine-server/tests/
uv run pytest packages/asr-core/tests/
uv run pytest packages/api/tests/
uv run pytest packages/client/tests/
uv run pytest packages/postprocess/tests/
uv run pytest apps/resona-cli/tests/

# Single test by name
uv run pytest -k test_transcribe

# Verbose output
uv run pytest -v packages/api/tests/test_endpoints.py

Root uv run pytest collects only the uv workspace (testpaths in the root pyproject.toml). The PWA in apps/resona-pwa has its own toolchain and runs in its own CI workflow (.github/workflows/pwa.yml):

just pwa test          # vitest (bun run test)
just pwa check         # eslint + nuxt typecheck
just pwa test-worker   # project worker, own uv env in apps/resona-pwa/worker

docs.title: Mocking strategy by package
docs.text:
Each package has a specific mock target. Using the wrong one leads to tests that pass in isolation but break under integration.

Package What to mock How resona-engine-server The transcriber singleton patch("resona_engine_server.app.get_transcriber", return_value=mock_t) resona-api The engine HTTP call respx.mock intercepting POST /transcribe on the engine URL resona-client The API HTTP call respx.mock intercepting calls to the resona-api base URL resona-cli CLI entry points typer.testing.CliRunner; patch client methods as needed resona-asr-core Entry-point discovery patch("resona_asr_core.registry.entry_points", return_value=[...])

docs.title: resona-engine-server
docs.text:
Mock at the singleton level so the FastAPI app never tries to load a real model:

from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from resona_asr_core.protocol import TranscriptionResult


@pytest.fixture
def mock_transcriber():
    t = MagicMock()
    t.transcribe.return_value = TranscriptionResult(
        text="raw transcript",
        language="de",
        segments=[{"start": 0.0, "end": 1.0, "text": "raw transcript"}],
    )
    return t


@pytest.fixture
def client(mock_transcriber):
    with patch("resona_engine_server.app.get_transcriber", return_value=mock_transcriber):
        with patch("resona_engine_server.auth.config", return_value=None):
            from resona_engine_server.app import app
            yield TestClient(app)

Also patch load_audio when sending raw bytes, so the audio parsing is bypassed:

import numpy as np
from unittest.mock import patch

def test_transcribe(client, mock_transcriber):
    with patch("resona_engine_server.app.load_audio", return_value=np.zeros(16000)):
        resp = client.post(
            "/transcribe",
            files={"audio_file": ("t.wav", io.BytesIO(b"\x00" * 100), "audio/wav")},
        )
    assert resp.status_code == 200

docs.title: resona-api
docs.text:
Use respx to intercept the outbound httpx call to the engine. The tests use a real in-memory SQLite database — see Never mock the database.

import respx
import httpx
import pytest

@pytest.fixture
def mock_engine(respx_mock):
    respx_mock.post("http://test-engine:9999/transcribe").mock(
        return_value=httpx.Response(
            200,
            json={"text": "hello", "language": "de", "segments": []},
        )
    )

The RESONA_ENGINE_URL env var in conftest.py is set to http://test-engine:9999 so all engine calls hit the respx mock.

docs.title: resona-client
docs.text:
Same pattern — use respx.mock to intercept calls to the resona-api base URL:

import respx
import httpx
from resona_client.client import ResonaClient


def test_get_job():
    with respx.mock:
        respx.get("http://localhost:7000/v1/jobs/123").mock(
            return_value=httpx.Response(200, json={"job_id": 123, "kind": "audio", "status": "completed"})
        )
        client = ResonaClient(base_url="http://localhost:7000", api_key="test-token")
        job = client.get_job(123)
    assert job.status == "completed"

docs.title: resona-cli
docs.text:
Use typer.testing.CliRunner to invoke commands without spawning a subprocess. Patch the client or engine at the point where the CLI constructs it:

from typer.testing import CliRunner
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
from resona_cli.main import app

runner = CliRunner()


def test_transcribe_calls_gateway(tmp_path):
    wav = make_wav(tmp_path / "a.wav")   # helper that writes a minimal WAV
    mock_client = MagicMock()
    mock_client.create_transcription.return_value = {
        "text": "hello", "language": "de", "segments": []
    }

    with patch("resona_client.client.ResonaClient.from_config", return_value=mock_client):
        result = runner.invoke(app, ["transcribe", str(wav)])

    assert result.exit_code == 0
    mock_client.create_transcription.assert_called_once()

docs.title: Never mock the database
docs.text:
resona-api tests use a real SQLite database

Do not mock Session, get_session, or any SQLModel function in resona-api tests. The test suite creates a real in-memory SQLite database via SQLModel.metadata.create_all(engine) in conftest.py and truncates all tables between tests. Mocking the DB layer hides real SQL errors and makes tests meaningless.

The conftest.py fixtures that make this work:

@pytest.fixture(scope="session", autouse=True)
def create_tables():
    from resona_api.db.engine import engine
    from resona_api.db.models import Job
    SQLModel.metadata.create_all(engine)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clean_db(create_tables):
    from resona_api.db.engine import engine
    with Session(engine) as session:
        session.execute(text("DELETE FROM job"))
        session.commit()

The environment variables in conftest.py must be set before any resona_api import, because paths.py and db/engine.py read them at module load time:

import os
import tempfile

_tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="resona_api_test_")
os.environ.setdefault("DATA_PATH", _tmp)
os.environ.setdefault("DATABASE_URL", f"sqlite:///{_tmp}/db/test.db")

docs.title: Audio fixtures
docs.text:
Keep audio fixtures small: 1–2 seconds, 16 kHz, mono WAV. Larger files slow down the test suite and add noise to diffs.

Place fixtures in <pkg>/tests/fixtures/:

packages/engine-server/tests/fixtures/sample.wav
packages/asr-core/tests/fixtures/silence.wav

Generate a minimal valid WAV in Python without any audio library:

import io
import struct
import wave


def make_wav(path, frames: int = 160, rate: int = 16000) -> bytes:
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    with wave.open(buf, "wb") as w:
        w.setnchannels(1)
        w.setsampwidth(2)
        w.setframerate(rate)
        w.writeframes(struct.pack("<" + "h" * frames, *([0] * frames)))
    data = buf.getvalue()
    path.write_bytes(data)
    return data

160 frames at 16 kHz = 10 ms — short enough to be negligible but valid enough for any WAV parser.

When you need a numpy array instead of bytes (for direct transcriber tests):

import numpy as np

audio = np.zeros(16000, dtype=np.float32)  # 1 second of silence at 16 kHz

docs.title: Dev Workflow
docs.text: This page covers the day-to-day development loop: how to install the workspace, run services, add dependencies, and know when you need to reinstall the tool.

docs.title: 1. Install all packages once
docs.text:
uv sync --all-packages

This installs every workspace package into .venv in editable mode. All Python source under src/ is live — changes to any package take effect the next time the process starts. The workspace root supplies the missing build dependencies for openai-whisper via [tool.uv.extra-build-dependencies], so no --no-build-isolation-package flag is needed.

docs.title: 2. Run everything through uv run
docs.text:
uv run resona transcribe ./audio/          # CLI
uv run resona-engine-faster-whisper        # engine server on :7001
uv run resona-api                          # API server on :7000
uv run resona rec                          # recorder TUI
uv run resona live                         # live transcription TUI
uv run resona ui                           # record-and-transcribe TUI

uv run resolves the workspace .venv. Because all packages are editable, your edits are visible immediately — no reinstall step needed.

docs.title: uv run vs uv tool install — comparison
docs.text:
uv run resona (recommended) uv tool install resona-cli Install mode Editable (live source) Copied into isolated tool env Workspace deps editable Yes — all packages No — only resona-cli itself when --editable is passed Pick up code changes Immediately (on next process start) Requires reinstall Use case Development and testing Verifying install personas Reinstall command n/a uv tool install --reinstall --from ./apps/resona-cli resona-cli

Tool install is not editable for workspace deps

Even if you pass --editable to uv tool install, only resona-cli itself becomes editable. Packages such as resona-postprocess and resona-asr-core are still copied, not linked. Use uv run resona from the repo root for all development work.

docs.title: Running individual services
docs.text:
# Terminal 1 — engine (requires GPU or falls back to CPU)
uv run resona-engine-faster-whisper

# Terminal 2 — API server (requires engine on :7001)
uv run resona-api

# Terminal 3 — CLI (talks to API on :7000)
uv run resona transcribe ./audio/

docs.title: Adding a dependency to a package
docs.text:
uv add --package resona-api httpx
uv add --package resona-cli typer

The --package flag scopes the addition to the named workspace member. After running this command, uv.lock is updated and the package is immediately available in the workspace venv — no extra sync step needed.

docs.title: Running the docs server
docs.text:
uv run mkdocs serve          # live-reload dev server at http://localhost:8000
uv run mkdocs build          # write static site to site/

docs.title: Checking what is installed
docs.text:
uv pip list | grep resona

All resona-* packages should show their source path (ending in /src) when installed editable.

docs.title: When you DO need to reinstall the tool
docs.text:
The installed tool (uv tool install) is only needed when you are verifying one of the install personas described in Installation. In that case, reinstall after every change:

# Default persona (CTranslate2 only)
uv tool install --reinstall --from ./apps/resona-cli resona-cli

# With PyTorch Whisper engine
uv tool install --reinstall --from ./apps/resona-cli 'resona-cli[whisper]'

# With Voxtral engine
uv tool install --reinstall --from ./apps/resona-cli 'resona-cli[voxtral]'

Note

The [whisper] and [voxtral] extras pull a PyTorch build from the cu130 index. uv tool install does not inherit the workspace index configuration, so these may fail to resolve torch outside the workspace. If that happens, stay in the workspace and use uv run resona instead.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Requirement Version Notes Python 3.12+ Required by all packages uv latest Package manager and workspace runner ffmpeg any recent Must be on PATH; used for audio decoding NVIDIA GPU + CUDA 12.8+ Required for local engine only; not needed for cloud-only or API-only use

docs.title: Workspace development install
docs.text:
Clone the repo and sync all packages in one step:

git clone https://github.com/ecsplico/resona.git
cd resona
uv sync --all-packages

The legacy openai-whisper package does not declare its build-time dependencies; the workspace root's [tool.uv.extra-build-dependencies] block supplies setuptools and wheel so uv sync succeeds without a manual --no-build-isolation-package flag.

Run commands through uv run while inside the workspace:

uv run resona transcribe recording.mp3
uv run resona-engine-faster-whisper   # starts engine server on :7001
uv run resona-api                     # starts API server on :7000

docs.title: Install personas (uv tool)
docs.text:
If you want an installed resona command outside the workspace, pick a persona:

Persona Command Default (record, live, local faster-whisper) uv tool install --from ./apps/resona-cli resona-cli Default + Whisper (PyTorch) engine uv tool install --from ./apps/resona-cli 'resona-cli[whisper]' Default + Voxtral (PyTorch) engine uv tool install --from ./apps/resona-cli 'resona-cli[voxtral]'

The default install is torch-free: it bundles faster-whisper via CTranslate2, so uv tool install completes without a GPU index.

PyTorch extras and the cu130 index

The [whisper] and [voxtral] extras depend on PyTorch from the cu130 index. uv tool install does not inherit the workspace's index configuration, so resolution may fail.

Workarounds:

  • Stay inside the workspace and use uv run resona <command> — the workspace index is always active.
  • Or install into a managed venv directly:
uv pip install \
  --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130 \
  'resona-cli[whisper]'

docs.title: macOS
docs.text:
The default persona (faster-whisper) is CPU-only and torch-free — it works out of the box on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs:

uv tool install --from ./apps/resona-cli resona-cli
resona transcribe recording.mp3

The [whisper] and [voxtral] extras pull PyTorch from a CUDA-Linux wheel index (pytorch-cu130) that has no macOS wheels — installing them straight will fail. Install PyTorch from PyPI first, then add the extra without the CUDA index:

uv tool install --from ./apps/resona-cli --with torch 'resona-cli[whisper]'
# or, for an existing tool environment
uv tool install --reinstall --from ./apps/resona-cli --with torch 'resona-cli[whisper]'

This installs the default PyPI torch wheel, which on Apple Silicon ships with MPS (Metal Performance Shaders) support. Resona's _detect_device() picks cuda → mps → cpu, so MPS is selected automatically when CUDA is not available and torch reports mps.is_available().

No CUDA on Mac

macOS has no CUDA support — the cu130 wheels would not work even if they were published for Mac. The MPS path is the only GPU acceleration on Apple Silicon.

docs.title: uv run resona vs installed resona
docs.text: uv run resona (workspace) resona (installed tool) Source Editable workspace packages Copied into tool environment Code changes Picked up immediately Requires re-install PyTorch extras Resolved via workspace index May require manual index flag Recommended for Development End-user deployment

docs.title: Local-Only Mode
docs.text: Local mode lets you transcribe audio or convert documents on this machine without a hub. It is explicit only: pass --local to resona transcribe, resona doc or resona watch. It is never chosen automatically.

docs.title: What works in local mode
docs.text: Operation Local Requires hub resona transcribe --local Yes — resona doc --local Yes — resona watch --local Yes — resona rec Yes — resona live Yes — resona transcribe / doc / watch without --local No resona-api (:7000) + resona-worker resona jobs, resona settings No resona-api (:7000) Profiles CRUD No resona-api (:7000)

docs.title: No automatic fallback
docs.text: Without --local the CLI always uses the hub. An unreachable hub, a timeout or a failed job is reported as an error (exit 1), and a policy denial exits with code 2. Nothing is ever retried locally or in the cloud.

docs.title: Settings and policy
docs.text:
--local runs the same policy path as hub admission:

  1. Settings come from the cache written by resona settings pull for the configured hub and credential (~/.resona/settings-cache/<hash>.json). Local mode never contacts the hub, so a used cache is marked stale: true. Without a cache, built-in private defaults apply.
  2. The execution profile (--execution-profile or the organization default) supplies the approved engine candidates; --engine/--model must match one of them.
  3. check_policy runs on every stage before processing. Cloud engines (deepgram, openai, elevenlabs) count as cloud egress and are denied unless the settings allow cloud and you pass --allow-cloud.
resona settings pull                                   # cache the hub's settings
resona transcribe recording.mp3 --local                # default execution profile
resona transcribe recording.mp3 --local --execution-profile cpu-private
resona doc scan.pdf --local --ocr force

docs.title: Execution
docs.text: The candidate runs in the worker's execution subprocess (resona-worker is a dependency of resona-cli) with the same private environment as on a worker: offline model caches and no credentials. Prepare model weights beforehand with resona-worker prepare; a missing model is reported as unsupported_capability.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
Local runs write the same outputs as hub jobs, next to the input by default:

recordings/
├── note-2026-05-17.mp3
├── note-2026-05-17.md
└── note-2026-05-17.result.json

Existing outputs are not overwritten without --force. Override the location with --output-dir:

resona transcribe ./recordings/ --local --output-dir ./transcripts/

docs.title: Postprocessing in local mode
docs.text:
--profile takes a profile name (looked up in ~/.resona/profiles/<name>.json), a path to a JSON file, or inline JSON — file and inline profiles are only accepted with --local. Without --profile, the cached organization settings decide whether the organization's postprocess profile applies. LLM steps pass the same policy check; cloud models are denied in private runs.

See Postprocessing for full pipeline documentation.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Get from zero to a transcript in three steps. No server required.

docs.title: Step 1: Install
docs.text:
uv tool install --from ./apps/resona-cli resona-cli

Or, if you have the workspace cloned:

uv sync --all-packages

See Installation for prerequisites and persona details.

docs.title: Step 2: Transcribe a file
docs.text:
resona transcribe recording.mp3

No server needs to be running. Resona spawns the faster-whisper engine in-process, transcribes the audio, applies default postprocessing (German dictation replacements), and exits.

You can also pass a directory, multiple files, or a glob:

resona transcribe ./recordings/          # all audio files in a directory
resona transcribe "recordings/*.mp3"     # quoted glob
resona transcribe a.mp3 b.mp3 c.mp3     # multiple files

GPU not required for cloud engines

If you don't have a local GPU, use a cloud engine instead:

export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
resona transcribe recording.mp3 --engine openai

docs.title: Step 3: Find the output
docs.text:
The transcript is written as a .txt file next to your input:

recordings/
├── dictation-2026-05-17.mp3
└── dictation-2026-05-17.txt   ← output

To write output elsewhere:

resona transcribe ./recordings/ --output-dir ./transcripts/

docs.title: What it looks like
docs.text:
$ resona transcribe dictation.mp3
Transcribing dictation.mp3 ...
  engine : faster-whisper (in-process)
  lang   : de (detected)
  took   : 4.2 s

Output : dictation.txt

The transcript has postprocessing applied — spoken punctuation commands like "Komma" and "Punkt" are replaced with , and . automatically.

First run downloads the model

On first use, faster-whisper downloads large-v3 (~3 GB). Subsequent runs use the cached model. Set DEFAULT_FASTWHISPER_MODEL=small to use a smaller model.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
The resona command is the main entry point for all end-user operations. It covers transcription, document conversion, directory watching, hub jobs and settings, TUI-based recording, live transcription, speech synthesis, and management of hub entries and postprocessing profiles.

Run resona --help or resona <subcommand> --help to see up-to-date flag descriptions at any time.

docs.title: transcribe
docs.text:
Upload one or more audio files to the hub as audio jobs and wait for the results.

resona transcribe [INPUTS...] [OPTIONS]

Accepted inputs

Form Example Single file recording.mp3 Multiple files a.mp3 b.mp3 c.mp3 Quoted glob "recordings/*.mp3" Directory ./recordings/

Supported formats: wav, webm, flac, mp3, m4a, ogg, aac.

Options

Flag Default Description --recursive / -r off Recurse into subdirectories; enables ** in glob patterns --output-dir DIR (input file directory) Directory for <stem>.md and <stem>.result.json --force off Overwrite existing outputs (otherwise they are never overwritten) --json off Print a parseable JSON report on stdout --no-wait off Submit and print job IDs; do not wait --timeout SECS (none) Seconds to wait per job; the job keeps running on the hub afterwards --private on Require private processing (the default) --allow-cloud off Allow cloud stages; mutually exclusive with --private and still requires the organization setting cloud_enabled=true --execution-profile NAME (organization default) Execution profile of approved engine candidates: private-auto, mac-private, linux-cuda, cpu-private --language LANG (organization setting) Language hint (ISO 639-1 code) --engine NAME (profile) Engine override; must match an approved candidate of the execution profile --model NAME (profile) Model override; must match an approved candidate of the execution profile --profile NAME (none) Stored hub postprocess profile name; a JSON file or inline JSON only with --local --instructions TEXT / --instructions-file PATH (none) User instructions for the profile's LLM steps (user message; the profile's prompt stays the system message).
