Needs a --profile with an llm/extract step. Also on resona doc and resona postprocess --translate off Translate to English --word-timestamps off Request word timestamps --diarize/--no-diarize profile default Label who spoke when; see Speaker diarization below --local off Process on this machine with cached hub settings instead of the hub

Outputs

Each input produces two files, written as a pair: both are staged first and a failure leaves neither new file (a file replaced under --force is restored). Inputs whose outputs would collide (same stem, e.g. a.wav and a.mp3, or same name from two directories with one --output-dir) stop the run with exit code 2 before any job is submitted.

  • <stem>.md — Markdown with YAML frontmatter (source, kind, job_id, language, engine, model, accelerator, execution_profile, private, worker, settings_revision, created_at).
  • <stem>.result.json — the job result (schema_version: 1: kind, raw_text, markdown, language, segments, pages, warnings, structured, provenance).

For every job one policy summary line goes to stderr, e.g. job 12: private=true execution_profile=cpu-private candidate=faster-whisper/large-v3@cpu status=completed.

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error or timeout, 2 policy_denied or colliding output names.

Speaker diarization

--diarize sets options.diarize on the job (hub and --local alike); --no-diarize turns it off explicitly. Without either flag the execution profile's diarize setting applies (off unless the organization set "diarize": true on that profile, e.g. for a conversation-recording profile). Only production audio jobs take the profile default; evaluation and testbench jobs never do. The result's segments are then speaker sections, each with a 1-based speaker number in order of first appearance, and the Markdown has one paragraph per section starting with **Sprecher N:** (job language de) or **Speaker N:** (other languages); long sections continue in further paragraphs without a label. The provenance gains a diarize stage. Only a worker whose prepare verified the diarizer takes such a job; until one is online it stays pending with queue_reason: no_capable_worker. An LLM polish step with preserve_markup keeps the raw chunk when the model drops, merges or renames a speaker label.

With --local, install the extra (uv tool install --from ./apps/resona-cli 'resona-cli[diarize]') and have the release's pinned Nemotron-3-Diarization weights in the HuggingFace cache: run resona worker prepare once, or hf download nvidia/Nemotron-3-Diarization --revision <pin> with the pin from resona_worker/models.json. The execution subprocess runs offline and never downloads them; without them the run fails with diarizer_unavailable.

Limits

  • On short recordings with several voices, speakers can be merged. On the synthetic de-case-conference fixture (4 voices, 81 s) the diarizer found 3 of 4 speakers, with 80.2 % of the words attributed to the right speaker and a DER of 31.3 %; on two voices (de-two-speakers) 98.3 % and 16.6 %.
  • At most 8 speakers (a limit of Nemotron-3-Diarization).
  • Engines without word timestamps (whisper.cpp, lightning-mlx) split speakers only at ASR segment boundaries, so a change inside a segment is missed.
  • A hub predating diarization ignores the diarize form field of /v1/audio/transcriptions: the result comes back without speaker labels and without an error. Jobs submitted through POST /v1/jobs (resona transcribe --diarize, MCP) fail there instead with 422 invalid_options.

Examples

# Transcribe a single file as a private hub job
resona transcribe dictation.mp3

# Transcribe a directory, writing output to a separate folder
resona transcribe ./recordings/ --output-dir ./transcripts/

# Pick an execution profile and an approved engine/model candidate
resona transcribe meeting.mp3 --execution-profile mac-private --engine mlx-whisper

# Submit only; check later with `resona jobs`
resona transcribe a.mp3 b.mp3 --no-wait

# Apply a stored postprocessing profile
resona transcribe dictation.mp3 --profile medical-de

# Allow cloud stages (organization must have cloud_enabled=true)
resona transcribe interview.mp3 --allow-cloud --language en

# Label speakers in a conversation
resona transcribe interview.m4a --diarize

# Explicit local run with cached hub settings and an inline profile
resona transcribe dictation.mp3 --local --profile '{"name":"x","steps":[{"type":"replacements","rules":[{"pattern":"Komma","replacement":","}]}]}'

No automatic fallback

The hub is configured with RESONA_API_URL or a hub entry in ~/.resona/config.json. An unreachable hub, a timeout or a failed job is reported as an error and never replaced by a local or cloud run; a policy denial prints policy_denied: ... and exits with code 2. An --engine/--model that is not an approved candidate is rejected with unapproved_override (exit 1). Cloud processing only runs on hub-approved non-private workers, never directly from the CLI; provider API keys in the environment never enable cloud.

--local

--local is explicit only, never automatic. It uses the settings cached by resona settings pull for the configured hub and credential (and marks the cache stale: true), or built-in private defaults when nothing is cached. The same policy check as on the hub runs before processing; the candidate runs in the worker's execution subprocess (resona-worker ships with resona-cli) using offline model caches. See Local-Only Mode.

Glob quoting

Always quote glob patterns to prevent shell expansion: resona transcribe "inbox/*.mp3".

docs.title: doc
docs.text:
Convert PDFs, images and Word documents (pdf, png, jpg, tif, docx) to Markdown as hub document jobs. A DOCX takes no OCR or page flags: --ocr other than off, --ocr-engine, --pages, --image-scale and --ocr-min-confidence are rejected (hub: 422 invalid_options); see Document options. Inputs, outputs, exit codes and the shared flags (--recursive, --output-dir, --force, --json, --no-wait, --timeout, --private, --allow-cloud, --execution-profile, --engine, --model, --profile, --local) work as for transcribe.

resona doc [INPUTS...] [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description --ocr MODE auto auto (OCR the layout regions without visible text; a visible, digital text layer is kept, an invisible OCR text layer is not counted as text, so those regions are OCRed again and the new OCR text replaces it), force (full-page OCR, any text layer ignored) or off (no OCR: the text layer as it is, an invisible one included) --ocr-engine NAME (profile) ocrmac, rapidocr or tesseract; must be available in the execution profile --languages LIST (alias --language) (organization setting) Comma-separated document languages: de, en, fr, it, es, ko --pages RANGE (all) Inclusive 1-based page range: a-b, a-, -b or a single page --image-scale X 1.0 1.0–4.0: multiplies the resolution OCR reads the page at (1.0 = 216 dpi, 2.0 = 432 dpi). Requires OCR --ocr-min-confidence X (engine default) 0–1: drop OCR text below this recognizer confidence. rapidocr only (its default is 0.5)

Not every OCR engine serves every language or option. A combination no worker can run fails the job (invalid_snapshot); a gap of one host (a missing tesseract pack) hands the job to another worker. Nothing is silently ignored:

ocrmac tesseract rapidocr de, en, fr, it, es yes if the deu/eng/fra/ita/spa pack is installed yes, one shared PP-OCRv6 recognizer ko yes if the kor pack is installed no: Korean weights are not bundled with the pinned rapidocr and jobs never download models --ocr-min-confidence no no yes (text_score)

--image-scale and --ocr-min-confidence require OCR (--ocr auto or force). Memory and OCR time grow with the square of the scale.

Measured on the evaluation corpus (gpu-box, rapidocr, 2026-11-02; CER = character error rate):

Fixture auto --image-scale 2 --ocr force force + scale 2 small print scan (7 pt, 150 dpi) 0.196 0.391 0.000 0.202 degraded scan 0.002 0.000 0.000 0.000 digital two-column page with table 0.000 0.000 0.263 0.265 digital three-column page 0.000 0.000 0.460 0.460
  • For a pure scan read by rapidocr, --ocr force is the best setting: auto OCRs each layout region as a separate crop, and the recognizer loses small print at crop edges.
  • Never use force on documents with a usable text layer: full-page OCR merges neighbouring columns and breaks reading order.
  • --image-scale 2 made small print worse with rapidocr. Raise it only after checking the result.
  • --ocr-min-confidence 0.3 and 0.7 changed no score.
  • ocrmac (Apple Vision, Mac worker) read every fixture of that corpus at CER 0.000, in auto too.
  • A scan under a garbled invisible text layer (bad-text-layer) scored like a plain scan in auto (0.004 rapidocr, 0.000 ocrmac): the bad layer does not reach the output.
  • French, Italian and Spanish scans (rapidocr, Mac CPU, 2026-11-04): auto 0.200 / 0.000 / 0.000, force 0.000 for all three. In auto, the French page lost most of its first line.
  • Korean (ko, ocrmac only, Mac, 2026-11-04): a rendered page of two Hangul lines (Apple SD Gothic Neo 26 px, light blur) read at CER 0.000 in auto and force. The corpus has no Korean fixture because rapidocr ships no Korean weights.
resona doc scan.pdf --pages 1-3 --languages de,en
resona doc ./faxes/ --ocr force --ocr-engine tesseract
resona doc small-print-scan.pdf --ocr force --ocr-engine rapidocr

docs.title: Page orientation
docs.text:
With OCR on (--ocr auto or force), every page in the range is turned upright before conversion, for every OCR engine. Tesseract's orientation detection (osd traineddata) reads each page at 200 dpi (about 0.3 s per page) and names the clockwise quarter turn that makes it upright; a turn below orientation confidence 2.0, or a page with too little text, leaves the page as it is. PDF pages are turned through their /Rotate entry (text layer untouched), images are rewritten turned. Each turned page adds the result warning page_rotated:<page>:<degrees> (clockwise), and the bounding boxes of its blocks refer to the upright page. --ocr off turns nothing.

Why: Docling runs layout, OCR and reading order on the page as scanned. An upside-down scan read by rapidocr came out with its lines in reverse order and a garbled last line; Apple Vision read the same simple page correctly. Detection read every page of the evaluation corpus and the engine test fixtures correctly in all four orientations (Mac, tesseract 5, 2026-11-10).

docs.title: postprocess
docs.text:
Run a postprocess profile on text without transcribing again: each input becomes a hub text job (see Text jobs) that runs only the profile. Outputs, exit codes and the shared flags (--recursive, --output-dir, --force, --json, --no-wait, --timeout, --private, --allow-cloud, --language, --local) work as for transcribe. There are no --execution-profile, --engine or --model flags.

resona postprocess [INPUTS...] --profile NAME [OPTIONS]
resona postprocess --job ID --profile NAME [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description INPUTS .md, .markdown or .txt files, globs or directories (UTF-8, at most 2 MiB each on the hub) --job ID Instead of files: re-run on the result of an earlier job. Input is its raw_markdown (the text before its own postprocessing), else its markdown; the language defaults to that job's. Outputs are job-<id>.<profile>.md + job-<id>.<profile>.result.json in --output-dir (default: the current directory), because the hub keeps no source file names; --json reports the input as job:<id> --profile NAME (required) Stored postprocess profile name; a file or inline JSON only with --local --instructions TEXT / --instructions-file PATH (none) User instructions for the profile's LLM steps, see transcribe

Outputs carry the profile in their name and sit next to the input unless --output-dir is given: resona postprocess notes.md --profile fix writes notes.fix.md + notes.fix.result.json, so the input is never replaced and runs of different profiles sit side by side. The profile part is the stored profile's name, a profile file's stem, or an inline JSON profile's name (postprocess if it has none), reduced to file-name-safe characters. Existing outputs are kept unless --force. --local runs the profile in-process with cached hub settings and the same policy checks; no execution subprocess is started.

# Re-run a new profile on job 12's transcript
resona postprocess --job 12 --profile transcript-markdown-de   # -> job-12.transcript-markdown-de.md

# Fix dictation commands in a note, next to it -> befund.fix.md
resona postprocess befund.md --profile fix

# Polish exported notes with the local LLM that only the assigned worker reaches
resona postprocess ./notes/*.md --profile document-polish-de --output-dir ./polished/

docs.title: watch
docs.text:
Watch a directory and submit each new audio file as a private hub job (or process it with --local). Writes the same two outputs as transcribe and skips files whose outputs already exist. Hub errors are reported per file and never replaced by a local run; a policy denial stops watching with exit code 2.

resona watch DIRECTORY [OPTIONS]

Options

Flag Default Description --recursive / -r off Watch subdirectories too --poll-interval SECS 1.0 Seconds between directory scans --output-dir DIR (input file directory) Directory for <stem>.md and <stem>.result.json --force off Re-transcribe files whose outputs already exist --execution-profile NAME (organization default) Execution profile (approved engine candidates) --language LANG (organization setting) Language hint --engine NAME / --model NAME (profile) Override; must match an approved candidate --profile NAME (none) Stored postprocess profile name (file/inline JSON only with --local) --local off Process on this machine with cached hub settings --diarize/--no-diarize profile default Label who spoke when, as resona transcribe --diarize

Examples

# Watch a directory, submitting new files to the hub
resona watch ./inbox/

# Watch recursively, poll every 5 seconds
resona watch ./inbox/ --recursive --poll-interval 5 --output-dir ./done/

docs.title: jobs
docs.text:
Inspect and manage hub jobs.

resona jobs get 12                      # job state as JSON
resona jobs wait 12 --timeout 300       # exit 0 completed, 2 policy denial, 1 otherwise
resona jobs result 12                   # print Markdown (--json for the full result)
resona jobs result 12 --output-dir out/ --stem interview   # write <stem>.md + .result.json
resona jobs cancel 12                   # fence the worker's lease
resona jobs delete 12                   # delete a terminal job's input, result and metadata
resona jobs list --limit 20 --cursor <cursor> --json

docs.title: testbench
docs.text:
Contribute recordings and scans to the hub testbench and list what it holds. Correcting references, bench runs and the leaderboard are done in the admin UI (/admin), not here.

resona testbench add memo.m4a scans/ --language de --label "Brief"   # files or directories; prints item id + status
resona testbench list --status needs_correction --kind audio --json   # org admin
resona testbench status                                               # enabled flag and counters

The organization must have testbench_enabled=true (the admin UI Testbench tab has an Enable button; CLI route in Testbench); otherwise add exits 1 with testbench_disabled and a hint. add exits 1 if any file was rejected.

docs.title: settings
docs.text:
Read and change the organization's revisioned settings on the hub (GET /v1/settings).

resona settings get                     # print current revision as JSON, refresh the cache
resona settings pull                    # cache the current revision for --local runs
resona settings get | jq .settings > settings.json   # edit the complete settings object …
resona settings set --file settings.json              # … and replace it on the hub

Settings are cached without secrets per hub URL and organization_id in ~/.resona/settings-cache/<hash>.json (hub_url, organization_id, credential — a SHA-256 prefix of the token, never the token —, revision, etag, settings, fetched_at, stale).

set takes only --file with the complete settings object (no key=value edits); it needs the org_admin role, validates the document against OrganizationSettings and sends If-Match with the cached revision. A 409 revision_conflict exits 1 with "run resona settings pull and retry". Changes apply to new jobs only; existing jobs keep their settings snapshot.

docs.title: rec
docs.text:
Launch the audio recorder TUI. Records from the default microphone and saves the audio file. Does not transcribe — use resona ui if you want to record and transcribe in one step.

resona rec

No options. The TUI shows recording time and allows stopping with a keypress.

Dependencies

Requires textual, sounddevice, and soundfile — all included in the default install.

docs.title: live
docs.text:
Launch the Resona Live TUI — the primary way to dictate. Each open document defaults to push-to-talk: tap F8 to record a segment, tap again to stop, and the transcript lands back in the buffer once ready (at the cursor position from when you started recording, or at the current cursor if you've since moved/typed elsewhere). Flip a document's Live switch (ctrl+l, or click it) to switch that document to continuous streaming transcription instead — confirmed text is spliced into the same buffer as you speak. Documents autosave as markdown after every insertion, on ctrl+s, and on quit.

resona live                # prompts for a filename, then opens it
resona live notes.md       # opens (or creates) notes.md directly
resona live --engine mlx-whisper --language en
resona live --remote http://api-host:7000 --engine deepgram   # cloud streaming (Live-only)
Option Description FILE (optional) Markdown document to open. Prompted for if omitted. --language, -l Transcription language (default de). --engine, -e Local engine to run in-process (default: fastest installed engine; on Apple Silicon lightning-mlx → mlx-whisper → whisper-cpp → faster-whisper). --remote, -r Stream to a remote server instead of running locally. Forces every document into Live mode — push-to-talk is local-only, same as recording audio needs a local mic either way. --debug Show a Logs tab capturing internal log output (useful for diagnosing engine/transcription issues).

Keybindings: F8 record/stop · ctrl+l toggle Live mode for the active document · ctrl+n new document (prompts for a filename) · ctrl+w close the active tab · ctrl+pagedown/ctrl+pageup switch tabs · ctrl+s save · ctrl+q quit.

Each document's audio segments and a manifest.json (transcript, status, insertion point per segment) are saved alongside it in a <name>.dictation/ directory.

Reuses an already-running local engine

Before loading its own in-process model, live checks http://localhost:7720/health (override the port with RESONA_LOCAL_ENGINE_PORT). If a resona-engine-* server is already running there, push-to-talk and Live mode both use it over HTTP/WebSocket instead of loading a redundant copy of the model.

docs.title: ui
docs.text:
Launch the record-and-transcribe TUI. Records audio, submits the file as a job to resona-api, and displays the result when the job completes.

resona ui

No options. Requires resona-api to be running at RESONA_API_URL.

docs.title: speech
docs.text:
Synthesise speech from text using a cloud TTS provider via the resona-api gateway.

resona speech TEXT [OPTIONS]

Options

Flag Default Description --engine NAME (gateway default) Engine name forwarded to the gateway --voice NAME alloy Voice name --model NAME tts-1 TTS model name --format EXT mp3 Output format: mp3, opus, aac, flac --speed FLOAT 1.0 Speech speed (0.25–4.0) --play off Play audio immediately via aplay/afplay/mpv --output PATH speech.mp3 Output file path; use - for stdout --private off Require a private engine

Examples

# Synthesise and save to speech.mp3
resona speech "Good morning, Dr. Schmidt."

# Use a specific engine and voice
resona speech "Hello world" --engine openai --voice nova

# Play back immediately without saving
resona speech "Appointment at three o'clock." --play

# Save to a specific file
resona speech "Processing complete." --output alert.mp3

# ElevenLabs with Rachel voice
resona speech "Bitte warten Sie." --engine elevenlabs --voice Rachel

# Pipe raw audio to stdout
resona speech "Test" --output -

See Speech Synthesis for full provider and format details.

docs.title: engines
docs.text: Manage built-in local engines and hub (resona-api) entries in ~/.resona/config.json.

docs.title: engines list
docs.text:
List all engines — built-in local engines plus configured hub entries from ~/.resona/config.json.

resona engines list

Output columns: NAME, TYPE, PRIVATE, STATUS.

docs.title: engines add
docs.text:
Add a hub (resona-api server) entry to ~/.resona/config.json.

resona engines add NAME API_URL [OPTIONS]
Flag Description --key KEY API key for server authentication --compose-dir DIR Docker Compose project directory — enables auto-start --ssh HOST SSH host to tunnel through --ssh-remote-port PORT Remote port on the SSH host

Examples

# Add a remote LAN server
resona engines add gpu-server http://gpu-machine:7001

# Add a server reachable over SSH tunnel
resona engines add home http://localhost:7001 --ssh user@homeserver.example.com

# Add a Docker Compose stack with auto-start
resona engines add local http://localhost:7000 --compose-dir ~/resona

docs.title: engines remove
docs.text:
Remove a configured engine entry.

resona engines remove NAME

docs.title: engines test
docs.text:
Test reachability of one or all configured engines. Exits with code 0 if at least one engine is reachable, 1 otherwise.

resona engines test             # test all configured engines
resona engines test gpu-server  # test a specific entry
resona engines test --timeout 5 # custom timeout in seconds

docs.title: engines status
docs.text:
Query the live resona-api gateway catalogue and show which engines are currently available, their capabilities, and their status. Requires a running gateway.

resona engines status

Output columns: Name, Kind, Capabilities, Available, Models.

docs.title: profiles
docs.text:
Manage postprocessing profiles stored on the resona-api server. A profile is a JSON file that bundles an initial_prompt list and an ordered pipeline of steps (replacements, LLM formatting, structured extraction). See Postprocessing Profiles for the full format.

Server required

The profiles subcommands communicate with resona-api. For local-only use, place profile JSON files in ~/.resona/profiles/ and reference them with --profile NAME.

docs.title: profiles list
docs.text:
List all profiles stored on the server.

resona profiles list

Output columns: NAME, DESCRIPTION.

docs.title: profiles show
docs.text:
Display the full JSON of a profile stored on the server.

resona profiles show my-profile

docs.title: profiles push
docs.text:
Upload a local profile JSON file to the server.

resona profiles push my-profile.json

The profile's name field determines the server-side name. If a profile with the same name already exists it is replaced.

docs.title: profiles pull
docs.text:
Download a profile from the server and save it to a local file.

resona profiles pull my-profile               # saves to my-profile.json
resona profiles pull my-profile output.json   # saves to output.json

docs.title: profiles delete
docs.text:
Delete a profile from the server.

resona profiles delete my-profile

docs.title: Engine Selection
docs.text: Hub jobs run on engines chosen by the job's execution profile — a list of approved engine candidates stored in the organization settings (seeded: private-auto (default), mac-private, linux-cuda, cpu-private). ~/.resona/config.json only lists the hubs the CLI talks to; built-in local engines run in-process for resona live and on workers.

docs.title: Built-in local engines
docs.text:
The following engines are always available without any configuration. They are loaded in-process (or as a subprocess if the optional extra is not installed).

Engine Package Backend Notes faster-whisper resona-engine-faster-whisper CTranslate2 INT8 Default, recommended, no PyTorch whisper resona-engine-whisper OpenAI Whisper (PyTorch) [whisper] extra required voxtral resona-engine-voxtral HuggingFace Transformers [voxtral] extra; supports Voxtral, Whisper-large, etc.

All built-in engines are always private — no audio leaves the machine.

docs.title: Model selection
docs.text:
Each engine has a default model and reads a corresponding environment variable:

Engine Env var Default faster-whisper DEFAULT_FASTWHISPER_MODEL large-v3 whisper DEFAULT_WHISPER_MODEL large-v3 voxtral DEFAULT_VOXTRAL_MODEL openai/whisper-large-v3

Override per invocation with --execution-profile, --engine and --model. The hub accepts an override only if it matches an approved candidate of the profile; otherwise it answers 422 unapproved_override and the CLI exits 1:

resona transcribe recording.mp3 --execution-profile cpu-private --engine faster-whisper --model medium

First-run download

Local engines download the model on first use (typically 1–3 GB). Subsequent runs use the cached model.

docs.title: Cloud STT providers
docs.text:
Deepgram, ElevenLabs and OpenAI are cloud engines. They are never private — audio is transmitted to the provider's servers. They run only on hub-approved non-private workers, for jobs submitted with --allow-cloud in an organization with cloud_enabled=true; the CLI never calls a provider directly, and provider API keys in the environment never enable cloud.

Provider Engine name API key env var (worker) Default model Deepgram deepgram DEEPGRAM_API_KEY nova-3 ElevenLabs elevenlabs ELEVENLABS_API_KEY scribe_v1 OpenAI Whisper openai OPENAI_API_KEY whisper-1

docs.title: config.json hub entries
docs.text:
Hub entries are stored in ~/.resona/config.json. Edit them with resona engines add or directly in the file (see Config Files).

{
  "engines": [
    {
      "name": "gpu-server",
      "api_url": "http://gpu-machine:7000"
    }
  ]
}

default_engine only selects the in-process engine for resona live.

docs.title: List engines
docs.text:
resona engines list

Output shows all built-in engines plus configured hub entries, with type and reachability.

docs.title: Add a hub entry
docs.text:
# Direct LAN connection
resona engines add gpu-server http://192.168.1.20:7000

# With SSH tunnel (port-forwarded automatically)
resona engines add home http://localhost:7000 --ssh user@myserver.example.com

# With Docker Compose auto-start
resona engines add local http://localhost:7000 --compose-dir ~/resona

docs.title: Test reachability
docs.text:
resona engines test               # all configured engines
resona engines test gpu-server    # one specific entry

docs.title: Show live gateway catalogue
docs.text:
Queries the running resona-api gateway for its current engine catalogue, including which engines are available right now and what they support.

resona engines status

docs.title: SSH tunnels and auto-start
docs.text:
SSH tunnels allow the CLI to reach a remote resona-api server by opening a port-forward. Configure with --ssh user@host:

resona engines add remote http://localhost:7000 --ssh user@myserver.example.com

The CLI opens ssh -L <local-port>:<host>:<remote-port> user@myserver.example.com when needed.

Auto-start via Docker Compose brings up the server locally when it is not reachable. Configure with --compose-dir:

resona engines add local http://localhost:7000 --compose-dir ~/resona

When the CLI detects the server is down, it runs docker compose up -d in the specified directory before retrying.

docs.title: Evaluation & Baselines
docs.text: resona eval runs every fixture of the committed evaluation corpus through one execution profile, scores the results and compares them with the promoted baseline for that profile and platform. A release reaches production only after an organization admin promotes a passing evaluation of it.

docs.title: The corpus
docs.text:
eval/corpus/ is synthetic and non-sensitive. Every file is generated by eval/corpus/make_corpus.py and licensed CC0-1.0. eval/corpus/MANIFEST.json lists, per fixture, the file, its SHA-256, the source, the license, the exact reference text, the checks that apply and optional job options.

Fixture Kind Checks de-speech German speech (macOS say -v Anna), umlauts WER, CER de-numbers German speech with numbers and dates WER, CER silence 6 s low-level white noise, no speech silence insertions (expected transcript is empty) digital-pdf German PDF with a text layer CER scan-pdf the same kind of text, rasterized (no text layer) CER table-columns-pdf 3×4 table page and a two-column page CER, required table cells, reading order degraded-scan-pdf two umlaut/ß-heavy paragraphs, 150 dpi raster rotated 1.5°, blurred, noisy, JPEG quality 35 CER small-print-scan-pdf 7 pt text rasterized at 150 dpi (tests the OCR image scale) CER dense-table-scan-pdf 6×6 ruled table with numbers, units and umlauts, raster only CER, all 36 table cells three-column-pdf digital page: title over three columns with headings CER, reading order bad-text-layer raster page under an invisible, deliberately garbled text layer (like a bad old OCR layer); default options CER fr-scan-pdf French paragraphs with é è à ç, raster only; job option languages: ["fr"] CER it-scan-pdf Italian paragraphs with à ì ò ù, raster only; job option languages: ["it"] CER es-scan-pdf Spanish paragraphs with ñ á é í ó ú ¿ ¡, raster only; job option languages: ["es"] CER de-two-speakers German doctor/patient consultation, 2 say voices (Anna, Flo) at their own rate and level, ~68 s, 18 turns, backchannels and early starts overlapping the previous turn; job option diarize: true WER, CER, speaker attribution, DER, speaker count de-case-conference German case conference, 3 say voices (Anna, Flo, Sandy) at their own rate and level, ~77 s, 19 turns, backchannels and early starts overlapping the previous turn; job option diarize: true WER, CER, speaker attribution, DER, speaker count

The hard fixtures (from degraded-scan-pdf on) are rendered with Bitstream Vera Sans, which ships with reportlab (Bitstream Vera Fonts license), so they do not depend on system fonts. bad-text-layer measures what a bad invisible layer does in the default auto mode. Docling does not count an invisible text layer as page text, so auto OCRs the page, and the OCR text replaces the garbled layer wherever OCR finds text; only ocr=off returns the layer. A visible, digital text layer is kept in auto. There is no Korean fixture: the bundled RapidOCR recognizer has no Korean weights.

docs.title: Per-fixture job options
docs.text:
A fixture may set options in the manifest, typed by its kind so the loader refuses invalid options (invalid document options / invalid audio options). They are merged over the default options of every evaluation job of that fixture, locally and with --remote:

  • Document fixtures take DocumentOptions, for example {"languages": ["fr"]} or {"ocr": "force"}, merged over the fixture language as languages. A document fixture without languages in its options needs a fixture language that is a document language.
  • Audio fixtures take AudioOptions, for example {"diarize": true}, merged over the defaults of a normal audio job (vad_filter on).

docs.title: Diarization fixtures
docs.text: A fixture with options.diarize carries its reference speaker turns: speakers: [{speaker, start, end, text}], in order of start. The generator mixes one say clip per turn, trimmed to its voiced span, so start/end are the exact sample span of that clip (rounded to 0.1 ms). Backchannels ("Mhm.", "Okay.") start 0.35 s before the previous turn ends, so the reference contains overlapping speech. The loader checks that the turn texts make up the reference, that only diarize fixtures carry speakers, and that the speaker checks (speaker_attribution, der, speaker_count) appear only on such fixtures.

docs.title: Corpus hash
docs.text:
The corpus hash is the SHA-256 of MANIFEST.json. The manifest pins the hash of every file, so the corpus hash covers files and references together. The loader refuses a corpus file that does not match its manifest hash.

Regenerate the corpus files:

uv run --no-project --with reportlab==5.1.0 --with pillow==12.2.0 --with numpy==2.2.5 \
    python eval/corpus/make_corpus.py --only hard

--only hard regenerates the hard document fixtures and is byte-reproducible with the pinned versions above. --only conversations regenerates the two diarization conversations (macOS German voices Anna, Flo and Sandy, each with its own speaking rate and level; seeded short gaps, long pauses, early starts, backchannel overlaps and noise, so it is reproducible on the same macOS version). --only base (or the default all) also regenerates the original fixtures and needs macOS with the German voice Anna and the system Arial; their bytes may differ on another macOS version, so leave them untouched unless they must change. MANIFEST.json is always rewritten from the files on disk; conversations that are not regenerated keep their reference turns from the current manifest.

Any change to the manifest changes the corpus hash. Every baseline must then be measured and promoted again (resona eval promote --rebaseline). Baselines promoted on an earlier corpus are no longer comparable and report baseline_required until they are promoted again. This happened when the hard fixtures were added, again when the French, Italian and Spanish scans replaced the duplicate bad-text-layer-force fixture, and again when the diarization conversations were added.

No private material

Do not add private audio, patient documents or transcripts derived from them to eval/corpus/. Keep operator corpora outside Git and outside public artifacts.

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text:
Scores are numbers only. Reports and hub records never contain transcripts or Markdown.

  • Audio fixtures are scored on the result's raw_text, the engine transcript before postprocessing.
  • Document fixtures are scored on markdown, because table structure and reading order exist only there. Postprocessing rewrites markdown and leaves raw_text as the converter produced it, so a plain run scores the converter's Markdown and a --postprocess-profile run scores the polished Markdown.
  • Normalization is versioned and recorded in every report:
    • text-v1: lowercase, ’ → ', non-word characters → space, whitespace collapsed. Umlauts are kept.
    • markdown-v1: HTML comments removed, then text-v1.
  • WER/CER use jiwer on the normalized text.
  • Silence insertions is the number of words emitted on the silence fixture.
  • Missing cells is the number of required cell values not found in a Markdown pipe table.
  • Order failures is the number of reading-order anchors that are not found after the previous anchor.
  • Speaker attribution (diarization fixtures, from segments[].speaker) is the share of reference words whose aligned hypothesis word (the text-v1 word alignment WER uses; equal and substituted pairs) carries the right speaker. Hypothesis speakers are mapped one-to-one onto reference speakers so that the most words count; a word of an unmapped or missing speaker is wrong. Higher is better.
  • DER is the time-based diarization error rate: missed speech + false alarm + speaker confusion over total reference speech, collar 0, overlapping speech scored, with the error-minimising one-to-one speaker mapping.
  • Speaker count error is |hypothesis speakers − reference speakers|. It is reported, not gated.
  • A diarization fixture whose result has no segments, or a segment without speaker, scores speaker attribution 0 and DER 1.0.

docs.title: The gate
docs.text:
Check Fails when Absolute any missing table cell, reading-order failure or silence insertion Regression any fixture's WER, CER or DER is more than 0.02 absolute above the baseline, or its speaker attribution more than 0.02 absolute below it Coverage a fixture or metric (including speaker_count_error) is absent from the baseline (baseline_required:<id>), or a baseline fixture was not evaluated (missing_fixture:<id>)

If no baseline exists for the profile and platform, or the baseline was measured on another corpus hash, the outcome is baseline_required. That is a nonzero exit, not a pass.

Exit codes: 0 passed (or measurement_only, see below), 3 gate failed, 4 baseline_required, 1 error, 2 policy denied.

docs.title: Local
docs.text:
resona eval --profile cpu-private --output-dir /tmp/resona-eval-cpu

Local mode runs each fixture through the explicit --local execution path (the same worker execution subprocess, private, organization polish disabled). It compares with the pinned entry in eval/baselines.json. Use it to check a machine before you enroll it. Local runs cannot be promoted.

docs.title: Against the hub
docs.text:
export RESONA_API_URL=https://resona.example.org
export RESONA_API_KEY=<org-admin token>
resona eval --profile mac-private --remote --output-dir /tmp/resona-eval-mac

--remote submits each fixture as a purpose=evaluation job. These jobs need an org_admin credential and the release_id of a release that is staged on the hub (default: the release from GET /v1/version; override with --release-id). Only workers that report exactly that release claim them. The CLI waits for the jobs, scores the results and records the summary with POST /v1/evaluations. Then it compares against GET /v1/baselines. The hub baseline is authoritative in remote mode; eval/baselines.json is not used.

Every run writes report.json to --output-dir: corpus hash, normalization ids, release, runtime versions, model revisions per stage, worker and accelerator per fixture, per-fixture metrics and the gate outcome.

docs.title: With a postprocess profile
docs.text:
resona eval --profile linux-cuda --remote --postprocess-profile <hub-profile> --output-dir /tmp/resona-eval-polish

--postprocess-profile sends the named hub postprocess profile as the job's profile with every document fixture; audio fixtures run without it. It needs --remote: local mode cannot resolve hub-stored postprocess profiles and refuses the flag. report.json records the name as postprocess_profile (null for plain runs).

Baselines measure the plain engines, so such a run is measurement-only: it is never compared with a baseline, it is not recorded on the hub (POST /v1/evaluations), and resona eval promote refuses its report. The absolute checks still apply: a missing table cell or reading-order failure exits 3; otherwise the outcome is measurement_only and the exit code is 0. Compare its per-fixture CER with a plain run's report to see what the polish changes.

docs.title: Promoting a baseline
docs.text:
resona eval promote <evaluation-id> --report /tmp/resona-eval-mac/report.json

Promotion calls POST /v1/evaluations/{id}/promote with the baseline revision that run saw as expected_baseline_revision. If another admin promoted in the meantime, the hub answers 409 baseline_revision_mismatch. The hub checks the gate again itself:

  • The first baseline (or the first on a new corpus) needs zero silence insertions, missing cells and order failures (422 absolute_checks_failed).
  • Later baselines must also pass the regression and coverage checks (422 gate_failed).

A successful promotion approves the (execution profile, platform, release) tuple for production jobs. The CLI then pins the entry in eval/baselines.json under <execution_profile>/<platform>: corpus hash, release, runtime versions, normalization ids, model revisions and per-fixture metrics. Commit that file.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
A worker's release is its installed resona-worker version, reported in its heartbeat. The hub's own release (RESONA_RELEASE_ID, else the resona-api version) is known without staging, but like every release it runs production jobs for a tuple only after an evaluation of that tuple has been promoted; a fresh hub therefore queues production jobs (queue_reason: release_not_approved) until its first promotion. Any other release must first be staged on the hub:

resona-admin release stage --manifest release-manifest.json

A staged release runs evaluation jobs only. It runs production jobs for a tuple after an evaluation of it has been promoted.

To compare engines on your own recordings and scans instead of the shared corpus, see the Testbench.

docs.title: MCP Server
docs.text:
resona-mcp exposes the hub's asynchronous job API to MCP clients (Claude, omp, SKAILE). It is a thin layer over resona-client: it never runs engines itself, and every call goes to the hub with an organization token, so privacy policy and organization isolation are enforced by the hub.

Two transports:

Mode Command Credential Local files Local stdio resona-mcp stdio RESONA_API_KEY from the environment only under RESONA_MCP_ROOT Hosted HTTP resona-mcp http --host H --port P Authorization: Bearer <org token> on every request never

docs.title: Tools
Local stdio
docs.text:
RESONA_API_URL and RESONA_API_KEY (an org client token from resona-admin credential issue) are required. path input is enabled only when RESONA_MCP_ROOT names an existing directory: the path (absolute or relative to the root) must resolve, after following symlinks, to a regular file inside the root. .. escapes, symlinks pointing outside the root, directories and URLs are rejected. Without RESONA_MCP_ROOT, path input is disabled and only create_upload_url, upload_content and upload_id work. There is no default root. Logs go to stderr; stdout carries only the protocol.

omp (~/.omp/agent/mcp.json) or Claude (~/.claude.json, mcpServers):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "resona": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "resona-mcp",
      "args": ["stdio"],
      "env": {
        "RESONA_API_URL": "https://resona.ecsplico.de",
        "RESONA_API_KEY": "<organization client token>",
        "RESONA_MCP_ROOT": "/Users/me/Dictations"
      }
    }
  }
}

From a workspace checkout, use "command": "/path/to/resona/.venv/bin/resona-mcp".

docs.title: Hosted Streamable HTTP
docs.text:
RESONA_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7000 \
RESONA_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS=resona.ecsplico.de \
RESONA_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://resona.ecsplico.de \
  resona-mcp http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 7010

The endpoint is /mcp (Streamable HTTP). resona_mcp.http:create_app() returns the same ASGI app for embedding; its lifespan runs the MCP session manager, so run that lifespan when mounting it inside another application.

  • Authentication. Every request needs Authorization: Bearer <org token>; missing or unknown tokens get 401. The server verifies the token against the hub (GET /v1/settings, so client and org-admin tokens work, worker tokens do not) and caches an accepted token for 30 seconds. Each tool call then uses that request's own token against the hub; the server has no key of its own. A token from another organization gets the hub's 404 for jobs it does not own.
  • Sessions. A protocol session is bound to the token that opened it. A session id presented with a different token is answered as if the session did not exist (404).
  • Input. Remote callers cannot pass path or URLs; use create_upload_url and send the file with curl, or upload_content for tiny files (request bodies up to 12 MiB, enough for 8 MiB of decoded content).
  • Host/Origin. Host must match RESONA_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS (421 otherwise) and a supplied Origin must match RESONA_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (403 otherwise). Both are comma-separated; host:* / scheme://host:* allow any port. Defaults allow loopback only.

Client configuration for a hosted server:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "resona": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://resona.ecsplico.de/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${RESONA_API_KEY}" }
    }
  }
}
Variable Mode Default Meaning RESONA_API_URL both stdio: required; http: http://127.0.0.1:7000 Hub base URL RESONA_API_KEY stdio required Organization client token RESONA_MCP_ROOT stdio unset (path input disabled) Directory local path inputs must stay inside RESONA_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS http loopback Allowed Host values RESONA_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS http loopback http:// origins Allowed Origin values

docs.title: Postprocessing Profiles
docs.text: After the ASR engine returns raw text, Resona applies a postprocessing profile. A profile is a JSON document that bundles vocabulary hints for the engine (initial_prompt) with an ordered list of pipeline steps that transform the raw transcript into the final output.

docs.title: Profile file format
docs.text:
{
  "name": "my-profile",
  "description": "German medical dictation with LLM formatting",
  "initial_prompt": ["Befund", "Diagnose", "Medikation"],
  "steps": [
    {
      "type": "replacements",
      "rules": [
        {"pattern": "\\bKomma\\b", "replacement": ","},
        {"pattern": "\\bPunkt\\b",  "replacement": "."},
        {"pattern": "\\bAbsatz\\b", "replacement": "\n\n"}
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "llm",
      "name": "format",
      "prompt": "Format this medical dictation as a structured clinical note with Markdown headings.",
      "model": "gpt-4o-mini"
    }
  ]
}
Field Required Description name yes Profile identifier (must match the filename when stored on disk) description no Human-readable description initial_prompt no List of phrases passed to the ASR engine as vocabulary hints steps no Ordered list of postprocessing step objects

docs.title: replacements
docs.text:
Applies a set of regex rules in order, case-insensitively.

Provide either rules (inline array) or source (path to a JSON rules file):

{"type": "replacements", "rules": [{"pattern": "\\bKomma\\b", "replacement": ","}]}

{"type": "replacements", "source": "my-rules.json"}

Each rule object:

Field Description pattern Regex pattern (case-insensitive, Python re syntax) replacement Substitution string; supports backreferences

docs.title: llm
docs.text:
Sends the current text to a language model and replaces the text with the model's response. Uses litellm — any OpenAI-compatible endpoint is supported.

Field Required Description type yes "llm" name no Human-readable label for this step prompt yes System prompt sent to the model endpoint no Id of an endpoint in the organization's settings registry; required in hub profiles model no litellm model string (overrides RESONA_LLM_MODEL; explicit local CLI mode only) api_base no Custom API endpoint (overrides RESONA_LLM_API_BASE; explicit local CLI mode only) timeout no Seconds per model call (default 120) chunk_chars no Process long Markdown in chunks of about this many characters (≥ 1000); never cuts a table. Enables max_attempts, max_length_deviation, preserve_markup 
{
  "type": "llm",
  "name": "structure",
  "prompt": "You are a German medical transcription assistant. Convert the following raw transcript into a structured clinical note with Markdown section headings.",
  "model": "ollama/llama3",
  "api_base": "http://localhost:11434"
}

LLM steps add latency. Use them only when rule-based replacements are insufficient.

For long documents, set chunk_chars. A chunk that keeps failing fails the job instead of being skipped; a chunk reply that changes the length too much or touches placeholders, headings or table shape is discarded, the raw chunk is kept and the result gets a polish_chunk_rejected:<n>:<reason> warning. Details: Postprocessing Pipeline. The bundled document-polish-de profile uses this mode for OCR correction of German documents. It calls the endpoint id local-llm, which names no host: an org admin registers a local_llm endpoint with that id and a loopback url on the approved worker; Linux Worker shows how.

When a step changes the Markdown, the job result keeps the engine's Markdown before postprocessing in raw_markdown; markdown is the postprocessed text.

docs.title: extract
docs.text:
Sends the current text to a language model and stores the model's structured JSON response alongside the transcript. The text is not modified.

{
  "type": "extract",
  "name": "icd_codes",
  "prompt": "Return a JSON object {\"codes\": [...]} listing all ICD-10 codes mentioned in the text.",
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini"
}

temperature, max_tokens and timeout apply as for llm.

Extracted data is stored in job.structured (server) or PostprocessResult.data (local).

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description RESONA_LLM_MODEL (unset) Explicit local CLI mode only: model for llm / extract steps that set no model. No default model; the hub never reads it RESONA_LLM_API_BASE (unset) Explicit local CLI mode only: API base for legacy LLM steps (e.g. local Ollama) RESONA_PROFILES_DIR <DATA_PATH>/profiles (server) / ~/.resona/profiles/ (CLI) Directory where named profile JSON files are stored

docs.title: default
docs.text:
When no profile is specified, the default profile bundled with resona-postprocess is used automatically. It turns German dictation commands into Markdown:

Spoken Written Komma , Punkt . Doppelpunkt : Fragezeichen / Ausrufezeichen ? / ! Absatz blank line (new Markdown paragraph) Anstrich new line starting with - (list item) Kapitel Titel ## Titel on its own line, followed by a blank line Klammer auf / Klammer zu ( / ) Eckige Klammer auf / zu [ / ]

Commands match whole words only: Zeitpunkt, Standpunkt and Kommandant stay as they are. Whisper often punctuates the commands itself (berichtet, Komma, er, Schmerzen. Punkt.); each punctuation command absorbs the punctuation right before and after it, so the result is berichtet, er and Schmerzen., never ,, or ... Commands never remove a line break, except Absatz, which becomes one.

Kapitel becomes a heading only when all of these hold:

  • the title has at most five words and no punctuation inside (a dot or comma between digits is fine, so Kapitel Diagnose F32.1 Absatz gives ## Diagnose F32.1); command words such as Komma never belong to the title;
  • the title is followed directly (an optional comma in between) by Absatz, Punkt, Doppelpunkt, Fragezeichen, Ausrufezeichen or by ., !, ?, : (a . next to a digit, as in 3. Mai, does not count);
  • Kapitel does not follow an article, preposition or ordinal (im, das, dem, vom, zum, letzten, …), so wie im Kapitel zuvor beschrieben. stays prose.

Otherwise the text stays exactly as spoken: Kapitel Anamnese der Patient berichtet Komma er habe Schmerzen Punkt becomes Kapitel Anamnese der Patient berichtet, er habe Schmerzen., not a heading. The medical section headings Verlauf, Medikation, Psychopathologischer Befund and Procedere (also spoken Prozedere) need no terminator; a spoken Absatz, Punkt, Doppelpunkt or Komma right after them is dropped. Leading and trailing blank lines are removed. The default profile also carries a few name corrections.

Zum Zeitpunkt der Aufnahme Kapitel Anamnese Absatz der Patient berichtet Komma er habe Schmerzen Punkt

becomes

Zum Zeitpunkt der Aufnahme

## Anamnese

der Patient berichtet, er habe Schmerzen.

Rules cannot tell a command from the same word used in a sentence. der wichtigste Punkt der Untersuchung becomes der wichtigste. der Untersuchung, Punkt eins becomes . eins, and im dritten Absatz starts a new paragraph. Dictate around these words, or correct them afterwards.

Behaviour change of the bundled default profile

Since the release that introduced the transcript profiles, default produces different output for the same audio: Absatz was a single newline and is now a blank line (new Markdown paragraph); Kapitel was # up to the end of the line and is now a terminated ## Titel heading (or nothing, see above); commands only match whole words (before, Zeitpunkt became Zeit.); Doppelpunkt, Anstrich and Eckige Klammer are new; doubled punctuation is merged. This affects every job that uses profile=default and every organization with polish on and postprocess_profile default.

The bundled default reaches the worker as a reference to default_replacements.json, which the worker resolves from its own installed resona-postprocess. Until every worker runs the new release, the same job can get old or new output depending on which worker claims it.

To keep the old rules, store them under another name (the name default is reserved) and select that profile (--profile, or the organization's postprocess_profile):

git show v0.1.0:packages/postprocess/src/resona_postprocess/default_replacements.json \
  | jq '{name: "dictation-v0-1", steps: [{type: "replacements", rules: .}]}' > dictation-v0-1.json
resona profiles push dictation-v0-1 dictation-v0-1.json

docs.title: transcript-markdown-de and transcript-polish-de
docs.text:
profiles/transcript-markdown-de.json holds the same dictation rules as default, without the name corrections and without any LLM step, so it runs on every worker. profiles/transcript-polish-de.json runs the same rules, then a chunked llm step on the endpoint id local-llm. Its prompt allows the model to change only capitalization (sentence starts, after headings, list items, nouns), punctuation and whitespace. It must not change, add or remove any word, not even a word that looks misrecognized; numbers, units, doses, drug names, diagnoses and codes stay exactly as transcribed. Settings: max_length_deviation 0.1, preserve_markup: true, temperature 0, chunk_chars 12000. Like document-polish-de, it needs an org admin to register a local_llm endpoint local-llm on the approved worker.

The guards check less than the prompt asks for. preserve_markup compares only HTML comments, the sequence of heading levels and the cell count of every table row; it does not notice merged paragraphs, joined list items, a rewritten heading text or a changed word or number. A reply that changes such things is kept as long as it stays within the 10 % length guard. Use the polish profile only where a reviewer reads the result.

Both carry their rules inline, because hosted profiles reject source. resona profiles push <name> <file> uploads a local JSON file, so take the file from the installed package. With uv tool install the package lives in the tool's own environment:

PROFILES="$("$(uv tool dir)/resona-cli/bin/python" -c "from importlib import resources; print(resources.files('resona_postprocess') / 'profiles')")"
resona profiles push transcript-markdown-de "$PROFILES/transcript-markdown-de.json"
resona profiles push transcript-polish-de "$PROFILES/transcript-polish-de.json"

In a repository checkout use packages/postprocess/src/resona_postprocess/profiles/ instead.

docs.title: LLM provider examples
docs.text: Cloud models (any step whose endpoint is not loopback) are denied in private runs. They need the organization setting cloud_enabled=true and a job submitted with --allow-cloud (the same applies to --local runs).

docs.title: OpenAI
docs.text:
{"type": "llm", "prompt": "Format this clinical dictation.", "model": "gpt-4o-mini"}

Requires OPENAI_API_KEY.

docs.title: Anthropic Claude
docs.text:
{"type": "llm", "prompt": "Format this.", "model": "anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku-20241022"}

Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

docs.title: Local Ollama
docs.text:
{
  "type": "llm",
  "prompt": "Format this clinical dictation.",
  "model": "ollama/llama3",
  "api_base": "http://localhost:11434"
}

In local CLI mode you can also set RESONA_LLM_MODEL=ollama/llama3 and RESONA_LLM_API_BASE=http://localhost:11434 globally.

docs.title: Server mode (resona-api)
docs.text:
Pass a profile field when submitting a job:

# Named profile (loaded from RESONA_PROFILES_DIR)
curl -F "audio_files=@dictation.wav" -F "profile=my-profile" http://localhost:7000/jobs

# Inline profile JSON
curl -F "audio_files=@dictation.wav" -F 'profile={"name":"x","steps":[...]}' http://localhost:7000/jobs

Manage named profiles with resona profiles:

resona profiles list
resona profiles push my-profile my-profile.json
resona profiles show my-profile
resona profiles pull my-profile my-profile.json
resona profiles delete my-profile

docs.title: CLI / local mode
docs.text:
# Named profile
resona transcribe dictation.mp3 --profile my-profile

# Inline JSON
resona transcribe dictation.mp3 --profile '{"name":"x","steps":[...]}'

# Default profile (no flag needed)
resona transcribe dictation.mp3

docs.title: Re-run a profile
docs.text:
Postprocessing normally runs inside an audio or document job, right after the engine. To apply a profile to text you already have, without transcribing again, submit a text job: the worker runs only the profile. Typical cases: a profile added after the transcript was made, or polishing with a local LLM that only its assigned worker can reach (the job is claimable only by that worker).

# Re-run on an earlier job's result (its text before its own postprocessing)
resona postprocess --job 12 --profile transcript-markdown-de

# Text or Markdown files
resona postprocess notes.md --profile document-polish-de --output-dir ./polished/

# On this machine, with cached hub settings
resona postprocess notes.md --profile my-profile.json --local --output-dir ./out/

The profile is required and must be stored on the hub (resona profiles push), except with --local. The result's raw_text is the input, markdown the profile output and raw_markdown the input when the profile changed it. Over HTTP: upload the UTF-8 text to POST /v1/uploads, then POST /v1/jobs with kind: "text" and profile (see Text jobs).

docs.title: Full profile example
docs.text:
{
  "name": "medical-de",
  "description": "German medical dictation with replacement + LLM structuring",
  "initial_prompt": ["Dr. Müller", "Befund", "Diagnose", "Medikation", "Procedere"],
  "steps": [
    {
      "type": "replacements",
      "source": "default_replacements.json"
    },
    {
      "type": "llm",
      "name": "structure",
      "prompt": "You are a German medical transcription assistant. Convert the following raw transcript into a structured clinical note with Markdown section headings (Verlauf, Medikation, Procedere). Preserve all clinical content exactly.",
      "model": "ollama/llama3",
      "api_base": "http://localhost:11434"
    }
  ]
}

In this profile:

  1. Spoken punctuation commands (Komma, Punkt, etc.) are replaced first.
  2. The resulting text is sent to a local Llama 3 model for structure and formatting.

Server-side postprocessing

When resona-api is running, profiles are stored in RESONA_PROFILES_DIR and applied server-side. The --profile flag on the CLI passes the profile name (or inline JSON) to the server with the job submission. In local (no-server) mode, profiles are resolved from ~/.resona/profiles/ or provided as inline JSON.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: For sensitive audio and documents — medical dictation, legal recordings, confidential meetings — it is important to ensure that data never reaches a third-party provider. Resona makes private processing the default and enforces it on the hub.

docs.title: What "private" means
docs.text:
A private job is processed entirely by engines and postprocess stages on machines you control (your own hub workers, or this machine with --local). No audio, document or text content (including the text of a text job and every intermediate transcript a postprocess step sees) is transmitted to any third-party cloud service.

A non-private job may use cloud stages that send data to an external provider's API (Deepgram, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, or a cloud LLM for postprocessing). Those requests are subject to the provider's data retention and privacy policies.

docs.title: Private by default
docs.text:
resona transcribe, resona doc and resona watch submit every job as private. --private is the default and only states it explicitly:

resona transcribe patient-notes.mp3 --private

The hub checks each job's policy before admission. A job whose execution profile, engine/model override or postprocess profile needs a cloud stage is rejected with policy_denied; the CLI exits with code 2. Nothing is ever retried on another engine, in the cloud or locally: an unreachable hub, a timeout or a failed job is reported as an error.

Each job prints one policy summary line on stderr, so the decision is visible:

job 12: private=true execution_profile=cpu-private candidate=faster-whisper/large-v3@cpu status=completed

docs.title: Allowing cloud processing
docs.text:
Cloud processing needs both:

  1. the organization setting cloud_enabled: true (set by an org_admin in the settings file passed to resona settings set --file settings.json), and
  2. --allow-cloud on the command (mutually exclusive with --private).
resona transcribe interview.mp3 --allow-cloud

Provider API keys in the environment never enable cloud. Cloud stages run only on hub-approved non-private workers, never directly from the CLI.

docs.title: resona-api hub privacy
docs.text:
The hub enforces the same policy for every entry point — POST /v1/jobs and the OpenAI-compatible POST /v1/audio/transcriptions adapter. private defaults to true; a private job is only leased to private workers, and a job that would need a cloud stage is rejected with 403 policy_denied.

# POST /v1/audio/transcriptions (private=true is the default)
curl http://localhost:7000/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESONA_API_KEY" \
  -F file=@patient-notes.mp3 \
  -F model=whisper-1

docs.title: Testbench contributions
docs.text: The optional testbench is the one place where the hub keeps content beyond the normal retention: contributed recordings and scans, their drafts, references and bench-run results are persisted until an org admin deletes the item. It is off by default (testbench_enabled), only org admins can read the stored content (the hub operator never can), and all testbench jobs are private, so nothing reaches a cloud provider. Contribute only material you have consent to keep.

docs.title: Practical recommendations for medical use
docs.text:
Medical and legal audio

Audio containing patient data, personal health information, or privileged communications should only be processed privately. Keep cloud_enabled=false for the organization so that even an accidental --allow-cloud is denied.

  1. Leave cloud_enabled off in the organization settings (resona settings get).
  2. Use a private execution profile (private-auto, mac-private, linux-cuda, cpu-private).
  3. Check the stderr policy line (private=true) or the private field in each <stem>.md.
  4. If you need cloud quality for non-sensitive content, an org_admin enables cloud_enabled and you pass --allow-cloud explicitly so the intent is visible in your command history.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Scenario Recommended setup Fully offline, no hub --local with built-in private defaults or cached settings Self-hosted hub Default (private) jobs; cloud_enabled=false Mix: private for sensitive, cloud for other cloud_enabled=true; pass --allow-cloud only for non-sensitive runs

docs.title: Resona app (Capacitor prototype)
docs.text:
Browsers stop the microphone when the phone is locked or the app goes to the background (WebKit bugs 226620 / 204681; Chrome on Android behaves the same). A web app cannot work around that. The Resona app is a Capacitor shell around the same Nuxt SPA (apps/resona-pwa) whose recordings run in a native recorder, so a recording keeps going while the screen is locked.

Status: prototype, Android first. iOS is prepared but not built or signed.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The app ships the static SPA build (nuxt generate → .output/public) as its web assets. Without a service worker: RESONA_CAPACITOR=1 disables @vite-pwa/nuxt.
  • Every recording flow asks useRecorder() (app/composables/useRecorder.ts) for a Recorder. Inside the app that is useNativeRecorder() (@capgo/capacitor-audio-recorder ≥ 8.4, format: "aac": ADTS AAC, audio/aac); in the browser it is useWebRecorder() (MediaRecorder). The upload → hub job flow behind it is the same: new recordings, push-to-talk on a recording, re-dictation and the /debug test dictation.
  • Android: on record, the app starts a foreground service of type microphone (@capawesome-team/capacitor-android-foreground-service) with the persistent notification "Resona nimmt auf", then starts the recorder. The service keeps the process alive, holds a partial wake lock and lets the app keep the microphone while locked. It stops when the recording stops. If the bridge reports that the service cannot start, the app refuses to record ("Hintergrundaufnahme konnte nicht gestartet werden."). The plugin resolves once it has asked Android for the service; a failure inside the service itself (startForeground) is only logged natively.
  • Elapsed time is computed from the wall clock, so the recording sheet shows the right length after unlocking (web view timers stall while locked).
  • Sharing a file from another app (Android share sheet → Resona) goes through a SEND / SEND_MULTIPLE intent filter and @capgo/capacitor-share-target into the same share page as the web share target (/share-target); see the Findings row "Share target".
  • On stop the app reads the recorded file back into the web view (Capacitor.convertFileSrc + fetch) and deletes it from the app cache; a file it cannot read stays in the cache.
  • Recovery after a kill (Android): ADTS is a stream of self-contained frames, so a recording the app never stopped stays readable up to its last whole frame (MPEG-4 writes its index only at stop). The recordings list scans cache/capacitor-audio-recorder/ for recording-*.aac files older than the running web view (app/data/nativeUnfinished.ts) and offers each like a web recording left in IndexedDB: "Nicht gespeichert …", Behalten → save sheet (upload → hub job) or Verwerfen. The file is deleted once saved or discarded; only its whole frames are uploaded. Nothing is offered while the plugin records; empty files are deleted; .m4a files of older app versions are left alone (unreadable without their index).
  • The hub sniffs ADTS by its frame sync (sniff_media, the MPEG audio branch) and admits it as an audio job; ffmpeg decodes it, a cut-off last frame included.

docs.title: Build the debug APK
docs.text:
Prerequisites: bun, JDK 21, Android SDK with platform 36 and build-tools. On macOS with Homebrew:

brew install openjdk@21
brew install --cask android-commandlinetools
export JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@21/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home
export ANDROID_HOME=/opt/homebrew/share/android-commandlinetools
yes | sdkmanager --licenses
sdkmanager "platform-tools" "platforms;android-36" "build-tools;36.0.0"

Build (the NUXT_PUBLIC_* values are baked into the bundle at build time):

cd apps/resona-pwa
bun install --frozen-lockfile
NUXT_PUBLIC_DATA_MODE=standalone \
NUXT_PUBLIC_RESONA_API_URL=https://<hub-host> \
  bun run cap:apk
# → android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk

cap:apk = cap:build (RESONA_CAPACITOR=1 nuxt generate && cap sync) + ./gradlew assembleDebug in android/. The native projects (android/, ios/) are committed; cap sync copies the web build and plugin list into them (both are gitignored).

The hub must allow the app's origin in CORS_ORIGINS: https://localhost on Android (capacitor://localhost on iOS). The bearer token still guards every call; CORS only lets the web view read the responses.

docs.title: Device test (Android)
docs.text:
Before: the hub has an online, approved worker and a promoted release for the organization's default execution profile (otherwise the job waits in the queue, queue_reason in resona jobs get).

  1. Install: adb install -r android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk, or copy the APK to the phone and open it (allow "install unknown apps" for the file manager).
  2. Open Resona → Einstellungen → Verbindung: enter the hub token.
  3. Tap record. Allow the microphone and notifications. The notification "Resona nimmt auf" appears.
  4. Speak, lock the screen, keep speaking now and then for 10 minutes.
  5. Unlock, open Resona (the notification opens it), note the elapsed time on the recording sheet, stop and save.
  6. Keep the app open until the recording shows its transcript: in standalone mode the queue is only processed while the app runs.
  7. Expected: the player's duration matches the elapsed time noted in step 5 (about 10 minutes), and the transcript covers what was said while locked.

Recovery after a kill:

  1. Start a recording, speak for about a minute.
  2. adb shell am force-stop de.ecsplico.resona (or swipe the app away / adb shell am kill after sending it to the background).
  3. Open Resona: the list shows "Nicht gespeichert: Aufnahme vom … (m:ss min)". Behalten → save; the transcript covers that minute. Afterwards adb shell run-as de.ecsplico.resona ls cache/capacitor-audio-recorder lists no file.
  4. A normal record → stop → save leaves no file there either.

Battery savers of some vendors (Samsung, Xiaomi, Huawei) kill foreground services anyway; if the recording ends early, set Resona to "unrestricted" battery use.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text: Area State Batch recording while locked (Android) Native recorder + microphone foreground service. Checked on an Android 15 emulator (debug APK, standalone mode): 180 s with the screen off, the service stayed in the foreground (type 0x80, wake lock held), the saved .m4a was 197 s long for 196 s shown on the recording sheet. Long recordings on a real phone (vendor battery savers, real mic) still need the device test above Push-to-talk, re-dictation Native recorder too; same upload → hub job flow Interruptions (#33) Web recorder only. Locking or backgrounding does not interrupt the native recorder (the service keeps the microphone), so it never shows "Aufnahme unterbrochen". A phone call does interrupt it, unnoticed: on Android 10+ the recording gets silence during the call and the plugin reports nothing; on iOS the plugin emits recordingInterruptionBegan/Ended, which the app does not handle yet, so the clock keeps running Recovery after a kill (#33, #40) Web recorder: IndexedDB chunks (resona-unfinished-recordings). Native recorder (Android): records ADTS (format: "aac", plugin ≥ 8.4), which stays readable up to its last frame; on the next open the recordings list offers recording-*.aac files left in cache/capacitor-audio-recorder/ (Behalten → save → hub job, or Verwerfen; the file is deleted either way). Unit-tested with plugin and Filesystem mocked, and ffmpeg decodes a cut-off ADTS file; the kill on a real phone (device test above) is still open. iOS: not offered (the plugin writes to the app's tmp/, which the scan does not read) Live dictation Foreground only, as in the browser. It streams PCM from getUserMedia over the /v1/listen WebSocket in the web view, and live.vue keeps useWebRecorder() for the audio of that same stream. Background live would need native PCM capture and a native WebSocket client Standalone data mode Works without login: IndexedDB + hub token; processing runs while the app is open Directus login Blocked as is. The SDK runs in cookie mode: the refresh token is an httpOnly cookie of the Directus host, and from the app origin https://localhost that is a cross-site cookie. The WebView accepts third-party cookies (Capacitor enables them), but Directus sets the refresh cookie SameSite=Lax (REFRESH_TOKEN_COOKIE_SAME_SITE in docker-compose.coolify.yml), so it is not sent on the app's cross-site refresh. Password login gets an access token, but the session ends at the first refresh (~15 min). Fix options: JSON auth mode in the app (refresh token in app storage), or SameSite=None refresh cookies on Directus. Either way Directus CORS_ORIGIN must also list https://localhost Keycloak SSO Blocked by the same cookie, plus the return: Directus redirects back to a web URL, not into the app. Needs the system browser (@capacitor/browser) + an app link / custom scheme deep link + a token handover Directus SSO does not offer today (it only sets the cookie) Nitro routes Not in the app (static build): calendar (/api/calendar), /api/debug-report, the /directus proxy. NUXT_PUBLIC_DIRECTUS_URL must be the absolute Directus URL Share target Android SEND intent filter on MainActivity for audio/*, PDF, PNG, JPEG, TIFF and DOCX, SEND_MULTIPLE for audio/*, application/* and image/* (Android gives several files their common type, */* when audio and documents are mixed, which matches too); @capgo/capacitor-share-target copies the files into the app cache and app/utils/nativeShare.ts stashes every usable one and opens /share-target: documents → uploaded at once, then audio → one save sheet (several recordings keep their file names as titles) → recordings; all wait for the hub token and become hub jobs. One file opens its page, several the list. Files of other types in a multi-share (GIF, XLSX, …) are skipped and reported; a single file of another type does not offer Resona. Tested on a Pixel 9a (Android 17) from the Files app: one memo (cold start), one PDF, one DOCX, two memos + a PDF in one share. DOCX needs a hub that accepts Word uploads (after 0.2.2). iOS would need a Share Extension + App Group (not set up) iOS Project generated (ios/, Swift Package Manager), UIBackgroundModes: audio and NSMicrophoneUsageDescription set. Not built: needs Xcode, an Apple developer account and signing

docs.title: Effort for iOS / TestFlight
docs.text:
• Apple developer account (99 USD/year), bundle id de.ecsplico.resona, signing in Xcode.
  • First build on a Mac with Xcode: bun run cap:build && npx cap open ios, set the team, run on a device. The recorder plugin keeps recording in the background with the audio background mode. Calls interrupt it: the plugin only resumes when iOS allows it (recordingInterruptionEnded.shouldResume), so the app has to handle those events (show the interruption, resume or stop) before iOS is usable; about half a day.
  • Hub CORS: add capacitor://localhost.
  • App Store review needs a privacy policy, the microphone purpose string (set) and a reason for background audio (dictation). TestFlight internal testing needs no review.
  • Rough effort: 1–2 days for a signed TestFlight build, more if login has to work (same blockers as Android).

docs.title: Text Replacements
docs.text: Text replacements convert spoken dictation commands into their written equivalents. They are a replacements step inside a postprocessing profile, applied after the ASR engine returns raw text. Matching is always case-insensitive.

docs.title: Bundled German dictation defaults
docs.text:
The bundled default profile applies these rules automatically with no configuration required:

Spoken Written Komma , Punkt . Absatz blank line (new Markdown paragraph) Kapitel Titel ## Titel (title ≤ 5 words, ends at Absatz/Punkt/. …; see Postprocessing) Klammer auf ( Klammer zu )

In addition, the bundled defaults include Doppelpunkt, Fragezeichen, Ausrufezeichen, Anstrich (list item), German medical section headings (Verlauf, Medikation, Psychopathologischer Befund, Procedere) and common name corrections.

Inspecting the defaults

The bundled rules live in packages/postprocess/src/resona_postprocess/default_replacements.json.

docs.title: Defining replacement rules in a profile
docs.text:
Replacement rules live inside a profile's replacements step. Provide them inline (rules) or point to a JSON file (source):

{
  "name": "my-profile",
  "steps": [
    {
      "type": "replacements",
      "rules": [
        {"pattern": "\\s*Komma",      "replacement": ","},
        {"pattern": "\\s*Punkt",      "replacement": "."},
        {"pattern": "\\s*Absatz",     "replacement": "\n"},
        {"pattern": "Monique",        "replacement": "Monic"},
        {"pattern": "Dr\\.\\s*Maier", "replacement": "Dr. Meier"}
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Or with a separate rules file:

{"type": "replacements", "source": "my-rules.json"}

Each rule object:

Field Description pattern Regex pattern (Python re syntax, case-insensitive). Backslashes must be doubled in JSON. replacement Substitution string; supports \n for newlines and backreferences.

docs.title: Capturing leading whitespace
docs.text: The ASR engine often inserts a space before each word. The pattern "\\s*Komma" matches both " Komma" and "Komma" and replaces the entire match with "," (no leading space), keeping punctuation attached to the preceding word. This is the recommended pattern for dictation commands.

docs.title: Medical section headings example
docs.text:
[
  {"pattern": "\s*Verlauf",    "replacement": "
## Verlauf
"},
  {"pattern": "\s*Medikation", "replacement": "
## Medikation
"},
  {"pattern": "\s*Procedere",  "replacement": "
## Procedere
"}
]

docs.title: Using custom rules
docs.text:
Create a profile with your rules and push it to the server:

resona profiles push my-profile.json
resona transcribe dictation.mp3 --profile my-profile

Or use it in local mode:

# Place the profile file in ~/.resona/profiles/
cp my-profile.json ~/.resona/profiles/
resona transcribe dictation.mp3 --profile my-profile

See Postprocessing Profiles for the complete profile documentation.

docs.title: Testbench
docs.text:
The testbench compares transcription and scan engines on your own recordings and documents. You contribute a file, correct the first result into a reference, run the item through several candidates and compare accuracy, time and device per candidate.

It is a hub feature, off by default, and only an organization admin can read what it stores.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. Contribute. Any client or org_admin credential adds a recording (audio) or scan (PDF/PNG/JPEG/TIFF): resona testbench add memo.m4a. The hub stores the original.
  2. Draft. The hub immediately queues a draft run: one job on the first available candidate for the file's kind. Its output is the first transcription or scan.
  3. Correct. An org admin opens the item in the admin UI, listens to or views the original, fixes the draft text and saves it as the reference (ground truth). The item is now corrected.
  4. Bench runs. The admin picks candidates (engine, model, accelerator) and runs the item through them. Each finished run is scored against the reference.
  5. Compare. The UI shows per-run metrics, a word-level diff against the reference, timing and device, and a leaderboard across all corrected items.

Item status: awaiting_draft (draft run not completed) → needs_correction (draft done, no reference) → corrected.

Correcting references, starting bench runs and the leaderboard are admin UI only; the CLI contributes and lists.

docs.title: Enabling it
docs.text:
The testbench is controlled by the organization setting testbench_enabled (default false). While it is off, every /v1/testbench/* route except /status answers 403 testbench_disabled. An org admin turns it on with the Enable testbench button on the admin UI Testbench tab, or from the CLI by editing the settings:

resona settings get | jq '.settings.testbench_enabled = true | .settings' > settings.json
resona settings set --file settings.json
resona testbench status

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
resona testbench add memo.m4a scans/ --language de --label "Arzt-Brief"   # contribute files / directories
resona testbench list --status needs_correction                           # org admin
resona testbench status                                                   # enabled, item/corrected/run counts

add prints <item id> <status> <kind> <file> per file (or --json). list accepts --kind audio|document, --status, --limit, --cursor, --json. The Python equivalents are the testbench_* methods of ResonaClient; the HTTP routes are in the API reference.

docs.title: Admin UI
docs.text: The hub's admin UI at /admin has a Testbench tab (org admin token): item list, original player/viewer, reference editor, candidate picker, run table with word diff, and the leaderboard.

docs.title: Candidates
docs.text:
