GET /v1/jobs/{id}/result/markdown returns one character range of the result's Markdown, never the whole result: {text, offset, next_offset, total_chars, source, kind, language, page_count, warnings, provenance}. offset ≥ 0 (default 0); limit 1–32768 characters (default 32768, larger → 422). source is markdown (default) or raw: raw reads raw_markdown (the text before postprocessing) when the result has one and markdown otherwise; the response's source names the field read (markdown or raw_markdown). next_offset is null once the range reaches the end; an offset past the end returns empty text. Concatenating text from offset 0 until next_offset is null reproduces that field exactly.

DELETE /v1/jobs/{id} works in every state. On a pending or processing job it also cancels the job: the lease is fenced, so the worker's next lease call returns 409 stale_lease and its result is rejected. The job, its idempotency keys, input and result files are gone at once; every later client read (GET, result, cancel, list, delete) answers 404. The hub keeps an invisible tombstone of a deleted processing job only until its lease would have expired, to fence the worker.

JobResult fields: schema_version, kind, raw_text, markdown, raw_markdown, language, segments, pages, warnings, structured, provenance. markdown is the final text. raw_markdown is optional (null or absent): it holds the engine's Markdown before postprocessing and is set only when a postprocess step changed it. For documents raw_text is the converter's plain text without tables, so raw_markdown is the unpolished reference. For audio raw_text is the engine's plain transcript; the worker builds markdown from segments: segment texts joined with spaces, a blank line between paragraphs. A paragraph ends at a pause of 1.5 s or more between one segment's end and the next start, or, once it is 1000 characters long, after the next segment ending a sentence (., !, ?, …, optionally followed by a closing quote or bracket); once it reaches 2000 characters, at the next segment. An engine without segment text yields markdown = raw_text. Postprocess profiles work on this Markdown, so with a profile markdown is the profile's output and raw_markdown the paragraphed transcript. For text jobs raw_text is the uploaded text, markdown the profile output, raw_markdown the uploaded text when the profile changed it, language the job's language; segments and pages stay empty and provenance has no engine stage. Results without the field stay valid; a hub older than this field rejects results that carry it (422 invalid_result), so update the hub before its workers.

docs.title: Job state machine
docs.text:
pending → processing → completed | failed | cancelled

A worker claims a job under a 120-second lease. If the lease expires, the job returns to pending. A job fails after three assignments (attempts_exhausted) or 24 hours (deadline_exceeded). Poll GET /v1/jobs/{id} or use ResonaClient.wait_for_job().

Retention: the input is deleted when the job reaches a terminal state, results after 24 hours, job metadata after 7 days.

docs.title: Worker routes (role worker)
docs.text:
Used only by resona-worker. Every call checks the organization, that the worker is approved and not revoked, and the current policy. A worker claims only jobs of its privacy class: private jobs go only to workers approved with --private, private: false (cloud opt-in) jobs only to workers approved with --non-private. A job whose postprocess or cloud ASR endpoint is assigned to a worker (worker_id in the endpoint registry) is claimable only by that worker, and POST …/policy denies (403 policy_denied) an endpoint assigned to another worker. Production jobs need a worker release approved for the job's (execution profile, platform) by a promoted evaluation; no release, including the hub's own, is approved without one. A claim poll never modifies jobs it cannot take; the maintenance sweep fails non-private jobs whose organization has since disabled cloud processing (policy_denied).

POST /v1/workers/heartbeat
POST /v1/workers/claim?wait=<0..25>
GET  /v1/workers/jobs/{id}/input        (X-Resona-Lease)
POST /v1/workers/jobs/{id}/heartbeat    (X-Resona-Lease)
POST /v1/workers/jobs/{id}/policy       (X-Resona-Lease)
POST /v1/workers/jobs/{id}/result       (X-Resona-Lease, X-Resona-Result-Sha256)
POST /v1/workers/jobs/{id}/fail         (X-Resona-Lease)

A call with an expired or replaced lease, or on a cancelled or deleted job, returns 409 stale_lease. An incompatible worker protocol returns 426. withdraw_capability in a fail body is recorded in the job's error message only: the hub never changes a worker's approved capabilities; the worker itself stops offering the withdrawn tuple until it is prepared again.

Heartbeat and claim bodies carry text_jobs: true from workers that run text jobs (every current resona-worker; no capability tuple is needed, so a worker whose tuples are all unusable still polls for them). A claim without it never receives a text job, so older workers keep working unchanged.

Likewise diarize: true comes only from workers whose prepare verified the speaker diarizer. An audio job with options.diarize is offered only to a claim carrying it; other claims skip it without touching the job. The hub stores the flag per worker (Worker.diarize, schema migration 7) for queue_reason. A false diarize is left out of the execution snapshot, so workers predating the option still run every other audio job. The heartbeat reply carries diarize: true to say the hub accepts the field in claim bodies; a worker sends it in a claim only after such a reply, because hubs predating diarization reject unknown claim fields (422). A worker whose diarizer stage fails (diarizer_unavailable, or out_of_memory in that stage) fails the attempt retryably without withdrawing its ASR tuple and stops reporting and claiming diarize until it restarts. Diarization limits.

Heartbeats carry features: the job features the worker's release knows, <kind>.<option> for every option field (document.remove_repeated_headers, audio.diarize, …) plus instructions (a postprocess profile with user instructions). A job is offered only to a worker that knows every option key in its execution snapshot's options and, when its profile carries instructions, instructions; other claims skip it without touching the job, and it waits as worker_outdated. The hub stores the list per worker (Worker.features, schema migration 8). Workers predating the field report none and are judged by their release (resona_job_core.features.LEGACY_RELEASE_FEATURES: 0.1.0 knows the first options, 0.2.0 adds instructions, 0.2.1 document.remove_repeated_headers, 0.2.3 audio.diarize; an unparseable release only the 0.1.0 set). The check applies to every job purpose (production, evaluation, testbench). A worker that still receives a snapshot with an option it does not know (from a hub predating the check) fails the attempt retryably as unsupported_options without withdrawing its tuple, instead of invalid_snapshot.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
GET /v1/settings      → {organization_id, revision, settings} + ETag
PUT /v1/settings      (org_admin, If-Match: <revision>)

docs.title: Management (/v1/admin, roles org_admin, hub_operator)
docs.text:
An org admin manages only its own organization: any other {org} returns 404 organization_not_found. A hub operator manages every organization. Worker and credential IDs of another organization return 404 (worker_not_found, credential_not_found), never 403. Other roles get 403.

GET  /v1/admin/me                                        → {role, organization_id, credential_id}
GET  /v1/admin/organizations                             → {items: [{id, created_at}]}  (org admin: own only)
POST /v1/admin/organizations          {id}               → 201 {id, created_at}  (hub_operator only; 409 conflict if it exists)
GET  /v1/admin/organizations/{org}/workers              → {items: [Worker]}  (active first, then by name)
POST /v1/admin/organizations/{org}/workers/{id}/approve {private: bool} → Worker
POST /v1/admin/organizations/{org}/workers/{id}/revoke  → Worker  (idempotent)
GET  /v1/admin/organizations/{org}/credentials          → {items: [{id, role, worker_id, created_at, revoked_at}]}  (newest first)
POST /v1/admin/organizations/{org}/credentials  {role: "client"|"org_admin"} → 201 {id, role, token}
POST /v1/admin/organizations/{org}/credentials/{id}/revoke → credential item
GET  /v1/admin/organizations/{org}/jobs?cursor=&limit=  → same page as GET /v1/jobs (metadata only)
GET  /v1/admin/organizations/{org}/settings             → {revision, settings}  (read-only)
GET  /v1/admin/organizations/{org}/baselines            → {items: [...], approved_releases: [...]}

Worker fields: id, name, approved, approved_private, online (seen within 90 s and not revoked), last_seen, runtime_version, revoked, reported_capabilities, approved_capabilities. Approval grants exactly the worker's reported capabilities: none reported → 409 no_reported_capabilities (run the worker once after resona-worker prepare); a revoked worker → 409 conflict. Partial approval stays with resona-admin worker approve --capabilities-file.

An issued token appears only in the 201 response; listings never contain tokens or hashes. Any other role in the body (including hub_operator) → 422. Revoking your own credential → 409 cannot_revoke_self; a worker credential → 409 use_worker_revoke (revoke the worker instead).

Baselines: one item per (execution profile, platform) with its highest revision, {execution_profile, platform, revision, evaluation_id, release_id, corpus_sha256, created_at}; approved_releases items are {execution_profile, platform, release_id, evaluation_id, approved_at}.

There are no admin routes for job results, cancel or delete: org admins cancel and delete through /v1/jobs/...; operators see job metadata only.

docs.title: Web page
docs.text: GET /admin serves a static management page (no build step at runtime, no external assets). Sign in with an org admin or hub operator token; the page keeps it in sessionStorage (resona-admin-token), so it is gone when the tab closes. Sections (hash routes such as #/workers): Overview, Workers, Credentials, Jobs, Settings, Baselines, Testbench. The page is built with IBM Carbon web components (Apache-2.0) and IBM Plex fonts (OFL), vendored as one prebuilt bundle into the hub package and served from /admin/vendor/carbon/ (carbon.js, carbon.css, fonts/*.woff2; rebuilt with packages/api/admin-vendor/build.sh); no CDN, external fonts or icon kits are loaded. Responses carry a strict Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'none', same-origin scripts, styles, fonts and requests only; blob: images and media for testbench previews), Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. /admin, /admin/admin.js and /admin/admin.css are sent with Cache-Control: no-store; the vendored bundle (.js, .css and .woff2 files only; .js/.css as their gzip twin when the client accepts gzip) with Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400. Any other /admin/… path, including paths that leave the vendor directory, → 404.

docs.title: List engines
docs.text:
GET /v1/engines

Returns the engines the caller's organization can use. Nothing is probed over the network. An audio/document engine appears when a candidate tuple of one of the organization's execution profiles is both approved for and reported as tested (prepared) by at least one approved, unrevoked worker of the organization. Cloud ASR candidates (deepgram, openai, elevenlabs) appear only when the organization has cloud_enabled=true and an approved cloud-asr:<provider> endpoint, and only through a non-private worker. Synchronous TTS engines of POST /v1/audio/speech follow the same cloud rule.

Response:

{
  "engines": [
    {
      "name": "mlx-whisper",
      "kind": "local",
      "job_kind": "audio",
      "capabilities": ["stt"],
      "private": true,
      "available": true,
      "models": ["mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-mlx"],
      "candidates": [
        {
          "candidate": {"engine": "mlx-whisper", "model": "mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-mlx",
                        "model_revision": null, "accelerator": "metal", "ocr_engine": null},
          "execution_profiles": ["mac-private", "private-auto"]
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "default": "mlx-whisper"
}
Field Type Description name string Engine identifier used in engine fields kind string "local" (runs on a worker) or "cloud" (provider) job_kind string audio, document or speech (TTS) capabilities string[] "stt", "document" or "tts" private bool true for local engines; cloud engines are always false available bool A worker offering it is online now (TTS: provider key set) models string[] Model names of the listed candidates candidates object[] Each approved tuple and the execution profiles that contain it

default is the engine of the first listed audio candidate of the organization's default execution profile, or null.

docs.title: Transcribe
docs.text:
POST /v1/audio/transcriptions
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

OpenAI-compatible speech-to-text, implemented as an adapter onto the job path. The hub never runs STT itself: it creates an audio job with the same admission and policy checks as POST /v1/jobs, then waits up to RESONA_SYNC_WAIT_SECONDS (default 60) for a worker to finish it. An optional Idempotency-Key header works as for POST /v1/jobs.

Field Type Required Description file file yes Audio file model string no whisper-1 uses the execution profile's default; anything else must be an approved candidate language string no Language hint (default: the organization's setting) response_format string no "json" (default), "text", or "verbose_json" prompt string no Accepted and ignored temperature float no Accepted and ignored engine string no Engine override; must be an approved candidate of the execution profile execution_profile string no Execution profile (default: the organization's default) profile string no Stored organization profile name; omit to use the organization default private bool no Default true; false needs cloud_enabled=true for the organization diarize bool no Default: the execution profile's diarize setting (off unless the organization turned it on); true labels speakers (AudioOptions.diarize), false turns it off: verbose_json segments carry speaker, the text has **Sprecher N:**/**Speaker N:** paragraphs. Part of the request an Idempotency-Key is matched against. A hub predating diarization ignores the field (unlabelled result, no error). Limits

Errors:

  • An override that matches no approved candidate: 422 unapproved_override.
  • A failed job returns its error code: 403 policy_denied, otherwise 502.
  • Timeout: 504 with Location: /v1/jobs/<job_id>; the job keeps running and its result can be fetched from the job routes.
{"error": "timeout", "message": "...", "job_id": 42}

With the Python client, ResonaClient.create_transcription(...) raises SyncWaitTimeout (with .job_id) on 504.

response_format responses:

// json (default)
{"text": "Das ist ein Test."}

// text
Das ist ein Test.

// verbose_json
{
  "text": "Das ist ein Test.",
  "language": "de",
  "duration": 3.2,
  "segments": [{"start": 0.0, "end": 3.2, "text": "Das ist ein Test."}]
}

// verbose_json with diarize=true: each segment is one speaker section
{
  "text": "**Sprecher 1:** Guten Tag.\n\n**Sprecher 2:** Hallo.",
  "language": "de",
  "duration": 2.4,
  "segments": [
    {"start": 0.0, "end": 1.1, "text": "Guten Tag.", "speaker": 1},
    {"start": 1.1, "end": 2.4, "text": "Hallo.", "speaker": 2}
  ]
}

docs.title: Synthesise speech
docs.text:
POST /v1/audio/speech
Content-Type: application/json

OpenAI-compatible text-to-speech. Only cloud engines support TTS; requesting a local-only engine returns 400.

Field Type Required Description input string yes Text to synthesise model string no Provider model override voice string no Voice identifier response_format string no "mp3" (default), "opus", "aac", "flac", "wav" speed float no Playback speed multiplier (provider-dependent) engine string no Engine name ("openai", "elevenlabs", "deepgram") private bool no Always false for TTS (cloud only)

Returns raw audio bytes with the appropriate Content-Type header.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
Postprocessing profiles are JSON files that bundle an initial_prompt list and an ordered pipeline of steps (replacements, LLM formatting, structured extraction). Named profiles are stored in RESONA_PROFILES_DIR on the server. The bundled default profile applies German dictation replacements automatically.

See Postprocessing Profiles for the profile file format.

docs.title: List profiles
docs.text:
GET /profiles/

Returns an array of profile summaries:

[
  {"name": "default", "description": "Bundled German medical dictation defaults"},
  {"name": "medical-de", "description": "German medical dictation with LLM formatting"}
]

docs.title: Get profile
docs.text:
GET /profiles/{name}

Returns the full profile JSON. Returns 404 if not found.

docs.title: Create or replace profile
docs.text:
PUT /profiles/{name}
Content-Type: application/json

Upload a profile object. The name field in the body must match the URL {name}. Returns the stored profile.

docs.title: Delete profile
docs.text:
DELETE /profiles/{name}

Returns {"ok": true}. Returns 404 if not found.

docs.title: Testbench
docs.text:
Contributed recordings and scans, references and bench runs. Disabled by default: with testbench_enabled=false every route except /status answers 403 testbench_disabled. hub_operator credentials are always rejected. See Testbench.

Method & path Role Description GET /v1/testbench/status client, org_admin {enabled, items, corrected, runs} GET /v1/testbench/candidates org_admin {items: [{kind, candidate, workers_online}]}: tuples approved and tested by ≥1 approved private worker POST /v1/testbench/items client, org_admin Multipart file (+ optional language, label). Persists the original, queues the draft run, 201 ItemDetail. 415 unsupported media, 422 empty, 413 over RESONA_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES GET /v1/testbench/items org_admin ?kind=&status=&limit=&cursor= → {items, next_cursor}, newest first GET /v1/testbench/items/{id} org_admin ItemDetail: summary + sha256, reference, draft, runs GET /v1/testbench/items/{id}/file org_admin Original bytes (inline, nosniff, no-store); 410 content_unavailable if the file is gone PUT /v1/testbench/items/{id}/reference org_admin Body {"text": "..."} (1–1,000,000 chars); sets the reference and re-scores completed runs DELETE /v1/testbench/items/{id} org_admin 204; removes row, files, runs and cancels active jobs POST /v1/testbench/items/{id}/runs org_admin Body {"candidates": [Candidate, ...]} (1–16); 422 unavailable_candidate for a candidate not in /candidates; an identical active run is skipped. 201 {items: [RunSummary]} GET /v1/testbench/items/{id}/runs/{run_id} org_admin RunDetail: text, warnings, alignment (null without reference or before completion) DELETE /v1/testbench/items/{id}/runs/{run_id} org_admin 204; cancels the job if active GET /v1/testbench/leaderboard org_admin {corrected_items, items: [{kind, candidate, items, wer_mean, cer_mean, seconds_mean}]} over completed bench runs on corrected items (draft runs excluded), best WER first

Item status is awaiting_draft, needs_correction or corrected; run status is queued, processing, completed, failed or cancelled; run role is draft or bench. Candidates have the job-core shape {engine, model, model_revision, accelerator, ocr_engine}. Audio runs are scored on raw_text with text-v1, documents on markdown with markdown-v1.

docs.title: Error responses
docs.text:
Status Meaning 400 Bad request (unknown engine, capability not supported, bad input) 404 Resource not found 409 Conflict (duplicate replacement or prompt; no engine available) 415 Unsupported media type 503 Engine unavailable; or cloud API key not set 502 Cloud provider returned an error

Error body:

{"detail": "human-readable message"}

docs.title: resona-asr-core
docs.text:
resona-asr-core is the lean shared foundation for all Resona ASR engines. It defines the Transcriber protocol that every backend must satisfy, the TranscriptionResult type they return, audio loading utilities, engine discovery and singleton management, and the LiveTranscriber for VAD-based streaming transcription.

This package has no FastAPI dependency and no web framework — it is a pure library imported by both engine packages and by resona-cli for in-process transcription.

docs.title: The Transcriber contract
docs.text:
All ASR backends implement the Transcriber protocol. You never need to instantiate a backend directly — use get_transcriber() which discovers and loads the engine registered under RESONA_ENGINE.

from resona_asr_core.registry import get_transcriber
from resona_asr_core.audio import load_audio

transcriber = get_transcriber()           # loads RESONA_ENGINE (default: faster-whisper)

with open("audio.wav", "rb") as f:
    audio = load_audio(f)                 # float32 mono waveform at 16 kHz

result = transcriber.transcribe(audio, language="de")
print(result["text"])
print(result["language"])
print(result["segments"])

docs.title: Engine discovery
docs.text:
Engines register themselves in their pyproject.toml under the resona.engines entry-point group:

[project.entry-points."resona.engines"]
faster-whisper = "resona_engine_faster_whisper.transcriber:FastWhisperTranscriber"

get_transcriber() uses importlib.metadata.entry_points to discover all installed engines at runtime and returns a thread-safe singleton. Set RESONA_ENGINE to select a non-default engine.

docs.title: Audio format
docs.text:
All engines expect audio as a mono float32 numpy array at 16 kHz. load_audio() handles conversion from any format that ffmpeg understands (mp3, wav, m4a, ogg, flac, aac, webm, ...).

SAMPLE_RATE = 16000  # Hz — the only sample rate accepted by engine backends

docs.title: Writing a new engine
docs.text:
Implement a class that satisfies Transcriber:

class MyEngine:
    def __init__(self, device: str, modelname: str | None = None) -> None:
        ...

    def transcribe(self, audio: np.ndarray, **kwargs) -> TranscriptionResult:
        ...

Then register it via pyproject.toml entry points and install into the workspace. get_transcriber("my-engine") will find it automatically.

docs.title: Transcriber
docs.text:
Bases: Protocol

Protocol that every Resona transcription backend must satisfy.

docs.title: TranscriptionResult
docs.text:
Bases: TypedDict

Return type for all transcriber backends.

docs.title: Audio utilities
docs.text: SAMPLE_RATE is the constant 16000. All engine backends expect audio resampled to this rate.

docs.title: load_audio(file, encode=True, sr=SAMPLE_RATE)
docs.text:
Read an audio file object as mono float32 waveform, resampling as necessary.

Decodes from an in-memory stream (ffmpeg pipe:). Non-seekable input means container formats whose index lives at the end of the file (non-faststart MP4/M4A) cannot be decoded — prefer :func:load_audio_path when a path is available. Raises RuntimeError if decoding yields no samples.

Source code in packages/asr-core/src/resona_asr_core/audio.py 
def load_audio(file: BinaryIO, encode: bool = True, sr: int = SAMPLE_RATE) -> np.ndarray:
    """Read an audio file object as mono float32 waveform, resampling as necessary.

    Decodes from an in-memory stream (ffmpeg ``pipe:``). Non-seekable input means
    container formats whose index lives at the end of the file (non-faststart
    MP4/M4A) cannot be decoded — prefer :func:`load_audio_path` when a path is
    available. Raises ``RuntimeError`` if decoding yields no samples.
    """
    if encode:
        try:
            out, _ = (
                ffmpeg.input("pipe:", threads=0)
                .output("-", format="s16le", acodec="pcm_s16le", ac=1, ar=sr)
                .run(cmd="ffmpeg", capture_stdout=True, capture_stderr=True, input=file.read())
            )
        except ffmpeg.Error as e:
            stderr = e.stderr.decode()
            log.error(f"FFmpeg error during audio loading: {stderr}")
            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to load audio: {stderr}") from e
        except Exception as e:
            log.error(f"Unexpected error during audio loading: {e}")
            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to load audio: {e}") from e
    else:
        out = file.read()

    return _pcm_to_waveform(out, sr)

docs.title: get_transcriber(engine=None)
docs.text:
Return the singleton transcriber, creating it on first call.

The engine argument selects which engine to load on the very first call. On subsequent calls the singleton is returned and engine is ignored. Call reset() first if you need to swap engines (intended for tests only).

Source code in packages/asr-core/src/resona_asr_core/registry.py 
def get_transcriber(engine: str | None = None) -> Transcriber:
    """Return the singleton transcriber, creating it on first call.

    The `engine` argument selects which engine to load on the very first call.
    On subsequent calls the singleton is returned and `engine` is **ignored**.
    Call `reset()` first if you need to swap engines (intended for tests only).
    """
    global _transcriber
    if _transcriber is None:
        with _init_lock:
            if _transcriber is None:
                _transcriber = _load_from_entrypoint(engine)
    return _transcriber

docs.title: reset()
docs.text:
Reset the singleton (for testing only).

Source code in packages/asr-core/src/resona_asr_core/registry.py 
def reset() -> None:
    """Reset the singleton (for testing only)."""
    global _transcriber
    _transcriber = None

docs.title: resona-client
docs.text: resona-client is the Python client library for talking to a resona-api server. It handles authentication, job submission, polling, and full CRUD for postprocessing profiles. Engine configuration — which servers to connect to, auto-start rules, and cloud provider registrations — lives in ~/.resona/config.json and is managed through EngineConfig and EngineEntry.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
resona-client is a workspace package. Add it from the monorepo:

uv add resona-client --package my-project

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
from resona_client.client import ResonaClient

# Connect using RESONA_API_URL / RESONA_API_KEY env vars (RESONA_API_KEY = org-bound token)
client = ResonaClient()

# Or use the resona-api entry in ~/.resona/config.json
client = ResonaClient.from_config()

# Upload + create job (private by default); returns JobRef(job_id, status)
ref = client.submit_job("recording.wav", kind="audio")
job = client.wait_for_job(ref.job_id)
if job.status == "completed":
    result = client.get_result(ref.job_id)
    print(result.raw_text)   # raw transcript
    print(result.markdown)   # after the postprocess profile

# Submit with a postprocess profile stored on the hub
ref = client.submit_job("recording.wav", kind="audio", profile="medical-de")

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> with every request when api_key is provided or RESONA_API_KEY is set. Tokens are org-bound and issued on the hub with resona-admin credential issue --organization <id> --role client. The hub derives the organization from the token; the client never sends a tenant identifier.

client = ResonaClient(base_url="https://resona.example.com", api_key="<token>")

docs.title: Job lifecycle
docs.text:
Jobs progress through pending → processing → completed | failed | cancelled. wait_for_job() polls until a terminal state and raises JobTimeout when its timeout passes; the job keeps running on the hub and the client never falls back to local processing. Each submit_job() call sends one Idempotency-Key and reuses it on retries, so a lost response cannot create a duplicate job.

ref = client.submit_job("dictation.mp3", kind="audio")
job = client.wait_for_job(ref.job_id, timeout=600)

if job.status == "completed":
    print(client.get_result(ref.job_id).markdown)
else:
    print("not completed:", job.status, job.error)

client.cancel_job(ref.job_id)   # fence the lease
client.delete_job(ref.job_id)   # any state: fence the lease, delete job, input and result now

get_result() raises JobNotReady (409) before completion and ResultExpired (410) after the 24-hour result retention.

To read a large Markdown result in bounded pieces, get_result_markdown(job_id, offset=0, limit=32768, source="markdown") returns a MarkdownChunk(text, offset, next_offset, total_chars, kind, language, page_count, warnings, provenance, source) from GET /v1/jobs/{id}/result/markdown; limit is at most 32 768 characters and next_offset is None at the end. source="raw" reads the unpolished raw_markdown when the result has one, else markdown; MarkdownChunk.source names the field read, and is None when the hub predates the parameter (such a hub ignores source="raw"). It raises the same JobNotReady/ResultExpired.

offset, parts = 0, []
while offset is not None:
    chunk = client.get_result_markdown(ref.job_id, offset=offset)
    parts.append(chunk.text)
    offset = chunk.next_offset

For content already in memory (the MCP server's upload_content), upload and submit in two steps; the upload is consumed by exactly one job:

up = client.upload_bytes("memo.wav", data)            # POST /v1/uploads → Upload(upload_id, sha256, size)
ref = client.submit_upload(up.upload_id, kind="audio", execution_profile="cpu-private")

docs.text:
Create a client by resolving the engine to use:

  1. RESONA_API_URL env var (if set) — used directly, no config lookup.
  2. WS_API_URL env var (if set) — used directly, no config lookup (fallback).
  3. With name: only that entry in ~/.resona/config.json, never another. Otherwise the first reachable entry.
  4. If none reachable and an engine has compose_dir set, start it via docker compose up -d and wait for it to become healthy.

Raises RuntimeError if no engine could be resolved.

Source code in packages/client/src/resona_client/client.py 
@classmethod
def from_config(
    cls,
    auto_start: bool = True,
    timeout: float = 3600.0,
    name: Optional[str] = None,
) -> "ResonaClient":
    """
    Create a client by resolving the engine to use:

    1. RESONA_API_URL env var (if set) — used directly, no config lookup.
    2. WS_API_URL env var (if set) — used directly, no config lookup (fallback).
    3. With ``name``: only that entry in ~/.resona/config.json, never another.
       Otherwise the first reachable entry.
    4. If none reachable and an engine has compose_dir set, start it via
       docker compose up -d and wait for it to become healthy.

    Raises RuntimeError if no engine could be resolved.
    """
    env_url = os.getenv("RESONA_API_URL") or os.getenv("WS_API_URL")
    if env_url:
        return cls(base_url=env_url, timeout=timeout)

    from .config import resolve_engine
    entry = resolve_engine(auto_start=auto_start, name=name)
    if entry:
        return cls(base_url=entry.api_url, api_key=entry.api_key, timeout=timeout)

    raise RuntimeError(
        "No reachable resona engine found.\n"
        "Add one with:  resona engines add <name> <url>"
    )

def submit_job(
    self,
    filepath: Path | str,
    *,
    kind: JobKind,
    execution_profile: Optional[str] = None,
    language: Optional[str] = None,
    engine: Optional[str] = None,
    model: Optional[str] = None,
    profile: Optional[str] = None,
    instructions: Optional[str] = None,
    options: Union[AudioOptions, DocumentOptions, Mapping[str, Any], None] = None,
    private: bool = True,
    idempotency_key: Optional[str] = None,
    provenance: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None,
    purpose: JobPurpose = "production",
    release_id: Optional[str] = None,
) -> JobRef:
    """Upload a file and create a job for it. POST /v1/uploads, then POST /v1/jobs.

    The Idempotency-Key is generated once per call (or taken from the argument)
    and reused for every retry of the job POST, so a lost response cannot create
    a duplicate job. The upload is not repeated; the retry reuses its upload_id.

    ``kind='text'`` uploads a UTF-8 text file and runs only the stored postprocess
    ``profile`` (required by the hub) on it; no execution profile, engine or model.
    ``instructions`` go to the profile's llm/extract steps as the user message.

    upload = self.upload(filepath)

        upload.upload_id,
        kind=kind,
        execution_profile=execution_profile,
        language=language,
        engine=engine,
        model=model,
        profile=profile,
        instructions=instructions,
        options=options,
        private=private,
        idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
        provenance=provenance,
        purpose=purpose,
        release_id=release_id,
    )

docs.text:
Create a job for an existing upload. POST /v1/jobs

The Idempotency-Key (generated unless given) is reused for every retry of the POST, so a lost response cannot create a duplicate job. purpose='evaluation' needs an org-admin credential and the release_id of a release staged on the hub (resona-admin release stage). instructions (user instructions for the profile's llm/extract steps) need a profile with such a step, else the hub answers 422 invalid_instructions.

Source code in packages/client/src/resona_client/client.py 
def submit_upload(
    self,
    upload_id: str,
    *,
    kind: JobKind,
    execution_profile: Optional[str] = None,
    language: Optional[str] = None,
    engine: Optional[str] = None,
    model: Optional[str] = None,
    profile: Optional[str] = None,
    instructions: Optional[str] = None,
    options: Union[AudioOptions, DocumentOptions, Mapping[str, Any], None] = None,
    private: bool = True,
    idempotency_key: Optional[str] = None,
    provenance: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None,
    purpose: JobPurpose = "production",
    release_id: Optional[str] = None,
) -> JobRef:
    """Create a job for an existing upload. POST /v1/jobs

    The Idempotency-Key (generated unless given) is reused for every retry of
    the POST, so a lost response cannot create a duplicate job.
    ``purpose='evaluation'`` needs an org-admin credential and the ``release_id``
    of a release staged on the hub (``resona-admin release stage``).
    ``instructions`` (user instructions for the profile's llm/extract steps) need a
    ``profile`` with such a step, else the hub answers 422 ``invalid_instructions``.
    """
    checked = _checked_options(kind, options)
    key = idempotency_key or str(uuid.uuid4())
    body: dict[str, Any] = {
        "kind": kind,
        "upload_id": upload_id,
        "private": private,
    }
    optional: dict[str, Any] = {
        "execution_profile": execution_profile,
        "language": language,
        "engine": engine,
        "model": model,
        "profile": profile,
        "instructions": instructions,
        "options": checked,
        "provenance": dict(provenance) if provenance is not None else None,
        "purpose": purpose if purpose != "production" else None,
        "release_id": release_id,
    }
    body.update({k: v for k, v in optional.items() if v is not None})

    resp = self._post_job(body, key)
    data = resp.json()
    return JobRef(job_id=int(data["job_id"]), status=str(data["status"]))

docs.title: wait_for_job(job_id, *, timeout=None, poll=1.0)
docs.text:
Poll until the job is completed, failed or cancelled.

Raises JobTimeout when the client deadline passes. The job keeps running on the hub; the caller decides what to do. Never falls back to local processing.

Source code in packages/client/src/resona_client/client.py 
def wait_for_job(
    self,
    job_id: int,
    *,
    timeout: Optional[float] = None,
    poll: float = 1.0,
) -> JobView:
    """Poll until the job is completed, failed or cancelled.

    Raises JobTimeout when the client deadline passes. The job keeps running on
    the hub; the caller decides what to do. Never falls back to local processing.
    """
    deadline = None if timeout is None else time.monotonic() + timeout
    while True:
        job = self.get_job(job_id)
        if job.terminal:
            return job
        if deadline is None:
            time.sleep(poll)
            continue
        remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
        if remaining <= 0:
            raise JobTimeout(job_id)
        time.sleep(min(poll, remaining))

def get_result_markdown(
    self,
    job_id: int,
    *,
    offset: int = 0,
    limit: int = 32768,
    source: Literal["markdown", "raw"] = "markdown",
) -> MarkdownChunk:
    """One character range of a completed job's Markdown.
    GET /v1/jobs/{id}/result/markdown

    ``limit`` is at most 32768 characters. ``source="raw"`` reads the result's
    ``raw_markdown`` (before postprocessing) when present, else ``markdown``;
    ``MarkdownChunk.source`` says which. Raises JobNotReady (409) before
    completion and ResultExpired (410) after retention.
    """
    params: dict[str, Any] = {"offset": offset, "limit": limit}
    if source != "markdown":
        params["source"] = source
    resp = self._send(
        "GET", f"/v1/jobs/{job_id}/result/markdown",
        params=params,
        expected={409: JobNotReady, 410: ResultExpired},
    )
    return MarkdownChunk.from_dict(resp.json())

def testbench_contribute(
    self,
    path: "Path | str",
    *,
    language: Optional[str] = None,
    label: Optional[str] = None,
) -> dict:
    """Contribute a recording or scan; the hub persists it and queues a draft run. POST /v1/testbench/items (client|org_admin)

    Raises ResonaAPIError with code ``testbench_disabled`` (403) while the
    organization has not enabled the testbench.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    data = {k: v for k, v in {"language": language, "label": label}.items() if v}
    content_type = mimetypes.guess_type(path.name)[0] or "application/octet-stream"
    with path.open("rb") as fh:
        return self._send(
            "POST", "/v1/testbench/items",
            files={"file": (path.name, fh, content_type)},
            data=data,
        ).json()

docs.text:
Transcribe audio through the OpenAI-compatible adapter. POST /v1/audio/transcriptions

The hub queues a normal audio job and waits a bounded time for a worker. model="whisper-1" means the execution profile's default; any other value is an override that must be an approved candidate. diarize=True labels speakers (only workers that diarize run the job), diarize=False overrides an execution profile that diarizes by default; None sends nothing (profile default). A hub predating diarization ignores the field: the result comes back without speaker labels and without an error (submit_job gets a 422 there instead).

Returns:

Type Description dict

Dict with key text (json and text formats).

dict

With response_format="verbose_json": text, language, duration, segments

dict

(each with speaker when diarized).

Raises SyncWaitTimeout (504) when no worker finished in time; the job keeps running and job_id identifies it for wait_for_job/get_result.

Source code in packages/client/src/resona_client/client.py 
def create_transcription(
    self,
    audio_path: "Path | str",
    *,
    model: str = "whisper-1",
    language: Optional[str] = None,
    response_format: str = "json",
    engine: Optional[str] = None,
    execution_profile: Optional[str] = None,
    private: bool = True,
    profile: Optional[str] = None,
    diarize: Optional[bool] = None,
) -> dict:
    """Transcribe audio through the OpenAI-compatible adapter. POST /v1/audio/transcriptions

    The hub queues a normal audio job and waits a bounded time for a worker.
    ``model="whisper-1"`` means the execution profile's default; any other value
    is an override that must be an approved candidate. ``diarize=True`` labels
    speakers (only workers that diarize run the job), ``diarize=False`` overrides an
    execution profile that diarizes by default; ``None`` sends nothing (profile default).
    A hub predating diarization ignores the field: the result comes back without
    speaker labels and without an error (``submit_job`` gets a 422 there instead).

    Returns:
        Dict with key ``text`` (``json`` and ``text`` formats).
        With ``response_format="verbose_json"``: ``text``, ``language``, ``duration``, ``segments``
        (each with ``speaker`` when diarized).

    Raises SyncWaitTimeout (504) when no worker finished in time; the job keeps
    running and ``job_id`` identifies it for ``wait_for_job``/``get_result``.
    """
    audio_path = Path(audio_path)
    data: dict = {
        "model": model,
        "response_format": response_format,
        "private": str(private).lower(),
    }
    optional = {
        "language": language,
        "engine": engine,
        "execution_profile": execution_profile,
        "profile": profile,
    }
    data.update({k: v for k, v in optional.items() if v})
    if diarize is not None:
        data["diarize"] = str(diarize).lower()
    content_type = mimetypes.guess_type(audio_path.name)[0] or "application/octet-stream"
    with open(audio_path, "rb") as f:
        resp = self._client.post(
            f"{self.base_url}/v1/audio/transcriptions",
            files={"file": (audio_path.name, f, content_type)},
            data=data,
        )
    if resp.status_code == 504:
        code, message = _parse_error_body(resp)
        job_id = _json_field(resp, "job_id")
        if code == "timeout" and isinstance(job_id, int):
            raise SyncWaitTimeout(resp.status_code, code, message, job_id=job_id)
    if resp.is_error:
        _raise_for(resp)
    if response_format == "text":
        return {"text": resp.text}
    return resp.json()

def resolve_engine(
    auto_start: bool = True,
    connect_timeout: float = 3.0,
    name: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Optional[EngineEntry]:
    """Return a reachable hub entry from ~/.resona/config.json.

    Args:
        auto_start: If True, try to start unreachable entries.
        connect_timeout: Per-entry reachability probe timeout.
        name: If given, resolve only the entry with this exact name.

    Entries are usable when /health responds; if not and ``auto_start`` is
    set, an SSH tunnel or docker compose project is started. A configured
    ``compose_dir`` that does not exist is logged and skipped instead of
    raising FileNotFoundError.

    Returns None if no usable engine is found.
    """
    cfg = EngineConfig.load()
    engines = cfg.engines
    if name is not None:
        engines = [e for e in engines if e.name == name]
    if not engines:
        return None

    # 1. Immediately reachable entries.
    for entry in engines:
        if is_reachable(entry, timeout=connect_timeout):
            return entry

    if not auto_start:
        return None

    # 2. Auto-start entries.
    for entry in engines:
        if entry.ssh_host:
            if entry.name not in _active_tunnels:
                proc = _start_ssh_tunnel(entry)
                _active_tunnels[entry.name] = proc
            host = _local_host(entry.api_url)
            port = _local_port(entry.api_url)
            log.info(f"Waiting for SSH tunnel to '{entry.name}' (up to 30s)...")
            if _wait_for_port(host, port, timeout=30.0) and is_reachable(entry):
                return entry
        elif entry.compose_dir:
            if not Path(entry.compose_dir).is_dir():
                log.warning(
                    f"Engine '{entry.name}': compose_dir '{entry.compose_dir}' "
                    f"does not exist — skipping auto-start."
                )
                continue
            _start_compose(entry.compose_dir)
            log.info(f"Waiting for '{entry.name}' to become available (up to 120s)...")
            if _wait_for_engine(entry):
                return entry

    return None

def is_reachable(entry: EngineEntry, timeout: float = 3.0) -> bool:
    """Return True if the engine's /health endpoint responds 200."""
    try:
        headers = {"X-API-Key": entry.api_key} if entry.api_key else {}
        resp = httpx.get(entry.health_url(), headers=headers, timeout=timeout)
        return resp.status_code == 200
    except Exception:
        return False

docs.title: resona-cloud-stt
docs.text:
resona-cloud-stt provides a thin, uniform interface for calling third-party speech-to-text APIs. Each provider module exposes a single transcribe() function with a consistent signature and return type. The registry resolves provider names to their modules and maps them to the env var that holds their API key.

The hub never calls providers itself: POST /v1/audio/transcriptions creates a job like POST /v1/jobs. Cloud STT runs only on hub-approved non-private workers, for jobs that allow cloud in an organization with cloud_enabled=true. You can also call the package directly from Python.

docs.text:
Provider Env var Default model Capabilities deepgram DEEPGRAM_API_KEY nova-3 STT elevenlabs ELEVENLABS_API_KEY scribe_v1 STT openai OPENAI_API_KEY whisper-1 STT

A worker offers a cloud STT engine only when its API key env var is set; the key alone never enables cloud processing.

docs.title: Direct usage
docs.text:
from resona_cloud_stt.registry import get_provider, PROVIDER_ENV_KEYS
import os

provider = get_provider("deepgram")

result = provider.transcribe(
    "recording.wav",
    api_key=os.environ["DEEPGRAM_API_KEY"],
    model="nova-3",
    language="de",
    options={},
)

print(result["text"])
print(result["language"])
print(result["segments"])   # list of {start, end, text} dicts

docs.title: resona-engine-server
docs.text:
resona-engine-server is a stateless FastAPI service that wraps one ASR engine and exposes it over HTTP and WebSocket. It has no database, no persistent state, and applies no postprocessing. Every request is self-contained.

  • Default port: 7001
  • Auth: optional RESONA_ENGINE_KEY env var
  • Engine selection: RESONA_ENGINE env var (default: faster-whisper)

Each engine package (resona-engine-faster-whisper, resona-engine-whisper, resona-engine-voxtral) points its [project.scripts] entry at resona_engine_server.run:main — the same FastAPI app, loaded with a different backend.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Set RESONA_ENGINE_KEY on the server to require an API key. When set, every request must include X-API-Key: <key>. Comparison uses secrets.compare_digest to prevent timing attacks. If the env var is unset, all requests are accepted.

Engine vs API key

RESONA_ENGINE_KEY guards the engine directly. The hub (resona-api) is guarded by org-bound tokens issued with resona-admin. In a standard deployment only the hub talks to the engine, so the engine key is an optional defence-in-depth measure.

docs.title: Health check
docs.text:
GET /health

Returns liveness status plus the active engine name and loaded model.

{
  "status": "ok",
  "engine": "faster-whisper",
  "models": ["large-v3"]
}

The model name is read from DEFAULT_FASTWHISPER_MODEL / DEFAULT_WHISPER_MODEL / DEFAULT_VOXTRAL_MODEL depending on the active engine.

docs.title: Transcribe (HTTP)
docs.text:
POST /transcribe
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

Transcribe a complete audio file and return the raw result. No replacements, no postprocessing — those are the caller's responsibility.

Field Type Default Description audio_file file required Audio in any ffmpeg-supported format task string "transcribe" "transcribe" or "translate" (translate → English) language string "de" BCP-47 source language hint initial_prompt string — Vocabulary hint prepended to the context vad_filter bool false Use voice-activity detection to skip silence word_timestamps bool false Include per-word timestamps in segments

Response:

{
  "text": "Das ist ein Test.",
  "language": "de",
  "segments": [
    {"start": 0.0, "end": 2.1, "text": "Das ist ein Test."}
  ]
}

When word_timestamps=true each segment contains a words array:

{
  "start": 0.0, "end": 2.1, "text": "Das ist ein Test.",
  "words": [
    {"word": "Das", "start": 0.0, "end": 0.3},
    {"word": "ist", "start": 0.3, "end": 0.5}
  ]
}

No md field

The engine response never contains md or postprocessed text. That is resona-api's responsibility.

docs.title: Streaming transcription (WebSocket)
docs.text:
WS /ws/transcribe

Chunk-based streaming transcription. The client sends audio in 2-second overlapping windows; the server returns partial transcripts as each window is processed.

docs.title: Client → Server messages
docs.text:
type Additional fields Description "audio" data (base64 PCM int16), sample_rate Append audio to the buffer "stop" — Flush remaining audio and end the session

Audio must be raw PCM int16, mono, at 16 kHz. Encode it to base64 before sending.

{"type": "audio", "data": "AAAA...", "sample_rate": 16000}

docs.title: Server → Client messages
docs.text:
type Additional fields Description "transcript" text, is_final Partial (is_final: false) or final (is_final: true) text "stopped" — Session fully stopped; all audio flushed "error" message Error during transcription "keepalive" — Sent every 10 s of client silence

The server accumulates audio in a rolling buffer. When the buffer reaches 2 seconds of audio, it transcribes that window (with 0.5 s overlap to avoid cutting words) and sends a transcript message. On "stop", any remaining buffered audio is transcribed as a final message.

docs.title: Live transcription (WebSocket)
docs.text:
WS /ws/live

VAD-based live transcription with partial/confirmed output. Uses LiveTranscriber from resona-asr-core, which detects speech boundaries and builds stable confirmed text incrementally.

docs.title: Client → Server messages
docs.text: type Additional fields Description "audio" data (base64 PCM int16), sample_rate Stream audio continuously "stop" — Flush remaining audio and close "config" language Change transcription language at runtime

docs.title: Server → Client messages
docs.text:
type Additional fields Description "partial" text, confirmed Current unstable hypothesis + stable confirmed portion "final" text Confirmed stable text for a completed utterance "stopped" — Session stopped; final confirmed text already sent "error" message Error during processing "keepalive" — Sent every 30 s of client silence

The confirmed field in "partial" messages grows monotonically — once text appears in confirmed it will not change. Only text (the unstable hypothesis) is subject to revision.

// Partial update — "das ist" is stable, hypothesis continues
{"type": "partial", "text": "das ist ein Test", "confirmed": "das ist"}

// Utterance boundary detected — full confirmed text emitted
{"type": "final", "text": "das ist ein Test."}

docs.title: CORS
docs.text: The engine server sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin from the CORS_ORIGINS env var (default *). Restrict this in production if the engine is exposed beyond resona-api.

docs.title: Model pre-loading
docs.text: On startup the engine server loads the ASR model before accepting requests (via FastAPI lifespan). If model loading fails (e.g. GPU out of memory), the server logs a warning and falls back to loading on the first request.

docs.title: resona-postprocess
docs.text:
resona-postprocess is the composable postprocessing library. It transforms raw engine output through an ordered pipeline of steps driven by a profile — a JSON document that combines vocabulary hints for the ASR engine with replacements, llm, and extract steps.

Postprocessing runs after the engine — never inside it. The hub validates a job's profile against the job's policy at admission; the worker runs the pipeline for every job (including jobs created through /v1/audio/transcriptions). resona transcribe --local applies it on this machine.

docs.title: Bundled default profile
docs.text:
resona-postprocess ships profiles/default.json. It is used automatically when no profile is specified and activates German medical dictation rules with no configuration needed.

Spoken Written Komma , Punkt . Absatz blank line (new paragraph) Kapitel Titel ## Titel (title ≤ 5 words with a terminator, see the postprocessing guide) Klammer auf / Klammer zu ( / ) Medikation, Verlauf, Procedere, ... Section headings

docs.title: Profile format
docs.text:
{
  "name": "my-profile",
  "description": "Optional description",
  "initial_prompt": ["phrase1", "phrase2"],
  "steps": [
    {"type": "replacements", "rules": [{"pattern": "\\bKomma\\b", "replacement": ","}]},
    {"type": "llm", "name": "format", "prompt": "Format this medical text.", "model": "gpt-4o-mini"},
    {"type": "extract", "name": "codes", "prompt": "Return JSON {\"codes\": [...]} with ICD codes."}
  ]
}

See Postprocessing Profiles for the full format reference.

docs.title: Direct usage
docs.text:
from resona_postprocess.profile import resolve_profile, bundled_default
from resona_postprocess.pipeline import build_pipeline, PostprocessResult

# Use the bundled default profile
profile = bundled_default()
result: PostprocessResult = build_pipeline(profile).run("Hallo Komma wie geht es Ihnen Punkt")
print(result.text)   # → "Hallo, wie geht es Ihnen."
print(result.data)   # → {} (no extract steps in default profile)

# Resolve a profile by name (from ~/.resona/profiles/ or bundled)
profile = resolve_profile("default", "~/.resona/profiles/")
result = build_pipeline(profile).run(raw_text)

# Inline profile
import json
profile = resolve_profile(json.dumps({
    "name": "x",
    "steps": [{"type": "replacements", "rules": [{"pattern": "hello", "replacement": "GOODBYE"}]}]
}), "/any/dir")
result = build_pipeline(profile).run("hello world")
print(result.text)   # → "GOODBYE world"

# Apply replacements directly (no pipeline needed)
from resona_postprocess.replacements import apply_replacements
rules = [{"pattern": "Komma", "replacement": ","}]
text = apply_replacements("Hallo Komma", rules)
# → "Hallo ,"

from resona_postprocess.llm import llm_transform, llm_extract

# Transform text via LLM: the endpoint must be approved by the policy
formatted = llm_transform(
    "Befund Absatz Patient kommt zur Kontrolle",
    prompt="Format this medical dictation text.",
    endpoint=endpoint,  # an Endpoint, e.g. kind local_llm with a loopback url

Each call runs check_policy immediately before the provider request. There is no implicit model, base URL or environment fallback inside these functions.

docs.text:
Ordered chain of text transforms and structured-extraction steps.

def __init__(self) -> None:
    self._steps: list[tuple[str, str, Callable]] = []

docs.title: run(text)
docs.text:
Run every step.

PolicyDenied and PostprocessStepFailed propagate; other failing steps are logged and skipped.

Source code in packages/postprocess/src/resona_postprocess/pipeline.py 
def run(self, text: str) -> PostprocessResult:
    """Run every step.

    ``PolicyDenied`` and ``PostprocessStepFailed`` propagate; other failing steps are
    logged and skipped.
    """
    result = PostprocessResult(text=text)
    for name, kind, step in self._steps:
        try:
            if kind == "text":
                out = step(result.text)
                if isinstance(out, StepOutput):
                    result.text = out.text
                    result.warnings.extend(out.warnings)
                else:
                    result.text = out
            else:
                result.data[name] = step(result.text)
        except (PolicyDenied, PostprocessStepFailed):
            raise
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            log.warning("Postprocess step %r failed, skipping: %s", name, e)
            result.data.setdefault("_skipped", []).append(name)
    return result

docs.title: build_pipeline(profile, *, policy)
docs.text:
Build a runnable pipeline. Every llm/extract stage is policy-checked here.

Raises :class:PolicyDenied before any processing if a stage is not allowed.

Source code in packages/postprocess/src/resona_postprocess/pipeline.py 
def build_pipeline(profile: Profile, *, policy: ExecutionPolicy) -> PostprocessPipeline:
    """Build a runnable pipeline. Every llm/extract stage is policy-checked here.

    Raises :class:`PolicyDenied` before any processing if a stage is not allowed.
    """
    endpoints: dict[int, Endpoint] = {}
    for idx, step in enumerate(profile.steps):
        if step.get("type") in LLM_STEP_TYPES:
            endpoints[idx] = _resolve_endpoint(step, policy)
    for idx, endpoint in endpoints.items():
        step = profile.steps[idx]
        check_policy(policy, [Stage(name=step.get("name", step["type"]), kind="llm", endpoint=endpoint)])

    pipe = PostprocessPipeline()
    for idx, step in enumerate(profile.steps):
        stype = step["type"]
        name = step.get("name", stype)
        if stype == "replacements":
            rules = _load_rules(step, profile.base_dir)
            pipe.add_text(name, lambda t, r=rules: apply_replacements(t, r))
            continue
        call = {
            "prompt": step["prompt"],
            "endpoint": endpoints[idx],
            "policy": policy,
            "settings": LlmCallSettings.from_step(step),
            "instructions": profile.instructions,
        }
        if stype == "extract":
            pipe.add_extract(name, partial(llm_extract, **call))
        elif "chunk_chars" in step:
            chunked = partial(
                llm_transform_chunked,
                **call,
                chunk_chars=step["chunk_chars"],
                step_name=name,
                max_length_deviation=step.get("max_length_deviation"),
                preserve_markup=step.get("preserve_markup", False),
            )
            pipe.add_text(name, lambda t, f=chunked: StepOutput(*f(t)))
        else:
            pipe.add_text(name, partial(llm_transform, **call))
    return pipe

docs.title: resolve_profile(ref, profiles_dir)
docs.text:
Resolve a profile reference to a Profile.

ref may be a Profile, a parsed dict, an inline JSON string, a filesystem path to a .json file, or a profile name resolved against profiles_dir. A file named <name>.json in profiles_dir shadows the bundled profile.

Source code in packages/postprocess/src/resona_postprocess/profile.py 
def resolve_profile(ref: Profile | dict | str, profiles_dir: Path | str) -> "Profile":
    """Resolve a profile reference to a Profile.

    `ref` may be a Profile, a parsed dict, an inline JSON string, a filesystem
    path to a .json file, or a profile name resolved against `profiles_dir`.
    A file named `<name>.json` in `profiles_dir` shadows the bundled profile.
    """
    profiles_dir = Path(profiles_dir)
    if isinstance(ref, Profile):
        return ref
    if isinstance(ref, dict):
        return Profile.from_dict(ref)
    if not isinstance(ref, str):
        raise ProfileError(f"Cannot resolve profile from {type(ref).__name__}")

    text = ref.strip()
    if text.startswith("{"):
        try:
            return Profile.from_dict(json.loads(text))
        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
            raise ProfileError(f"Invalid inline profile JSON: {e}") from e

    path = Path(ref)
    if path.suffix == ".json" and path.exists():
        return Profile.from_file(path)

    candidate = profiles_dir / f"{ref}.json"
    if candidate.exists():
        return Profile.from_file(candidate)
    if ref == "default":
        return bundled_default()
    raise ProfileError(f"Profile not found: {ref}")

docs.text:
Return the default profile bundled with resona-postprocess.

Raises ProfileError if the bundled file is missing or unparseable.

Source code in packages/postprocess/src/resona_postprocess/profile.py 
def bundled_default() -> "Profile":
    """Return the `default` profile bundled with resona-postprocess.

    Raises ProfileError if the bundled file is missing or unparseable.
    """
    try:
        ref = resources.files("resona_postprocess").joinpath("profiles/default.json")
        data = json.loads(ref.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        raise ProfileError(f"Cannot load bundled default profile: {e}") from e
    # base_dir=None: a 'source' of 'default_replacements.json' resolves via the
    # bundled-resource fallback in pipeline._load_rules.
    return Profile.from_dict(data, base_dir=None)

docs.title: list_profiles(profiles_dir)
docs.text:
List {name, description} for every profile file in profiles_dir.

Source code in packages/postprocess/src/resona_postprocess/profile.py 
def list_profiles(profiles_dir: Path | str) -> list[dict]:
    """List `{name, description}` for every profile file in `profiles_dir`."""
    profiles_dir = Path(profiles_dir)
    out: list[dict] = []
    if not profiles_dir.is_dir():
        return out
    for path in sorted(profiles_dir.glob("*.json")):
        try:
            p = Profile.from_file(path)
            out.append({"name": p.name, "description": p.description})
        except ProfileError:
            continue
    return out

docs.title: apply_replacements(text, replacements)
docs.text:
Apply a list of regex replacements to text in order.

Each rule provides the regex under pattern (preferred) or the legacy name key, plus replacement. Invalid patterns are logged and skipped.

Source code in packages/postprocess/src/resona_postprocess/replacements.py 
def apply_replacements(text: str, replacements: list[dict[str, str]]) -> str:
    """Apply a list of regex replacements to text in order.

    Each rule provides the regex under ``pattern`` (preferred) or the legacy
    ``name`` key, plus ``replacement``. Invalid patterns are logged and skipped.
    """
    for r in replacements:
        pattern = r.get("pattern", r.get("name"))
        if pattern is None:
            log.warning("Replacement rule missing 'pattern'/'name': %r", r)
            continue
        try:
            new_text, n = re.compile(pattern, re.IGNORECASE).subn(
                r.get("replacement", ""), text
            )
            if n > 0:
                text = new_text
        except re.error as e:
            log.warning(f"Invalid replacement pattern '{pattern}': {e}")
    return text

docs.title: llm_transform(text, *, prompt, endpoint, policy, settings=LlmCallSettings(), instructions=None)
docs.text:
Send transcript text to an approved LLM endpoint and return the result.

The policy is checked on every call, before litellm is reached. The endpoint fixes the model and base URL; no environment fallback applies here.

Source code in packages/postprocess/src/resona_postprocess/llm.py 
def llm_transform(
    text: str,
    *,
    prompt: str,
    endpoint: Endpoint,
    policy: ExecutionPolicy,
    settings: LlmCallSettings = LlmCallSettings(),
    instructions: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Send transcript text to an approved LLM endpoint and return the result.

    The policy is checked on every call, before litellm is reached. The endpoint
    fixes the model and base URL; no environment fallback applies here.
    """
    check_policy(policy, [Stage(name="llm", kind="llm", endpoint=endpoint)])
    reply = _completion(endpoint=endpoint, messages=_messages(prompt, text, instructions), settings=settings)
    return _unwrap_text(reply) if instructions is not None and reply else reply

docs.title: llm_extract(text, *, prompt, endpoint, policy, settings=LlmCallSettings(), instructions=None)
docs.text:
Extract structured data from text. Returns a parsed JSON object.

On a malformed LLM response, returns {"_raw": <response string>} so a job never hard-fails on a bad extraction.

Source code in packages/postprocess/src/resona_postprocess/llm.py 
def llm_extract(
    text: str,
    *,
    prompt: str,
    endpoint: Endpoint,
    policy: ExecutionPolicy,
    settings: LlmCallSettings = LlmCallSettings(),
    instructions: str | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Extract structured data from text. Returns a parsed JSON object.

    On a malformed LLM response, returns ``{"_raw": <response string>}`` so a
    job never hard-fails on a bad extraction.
    """
    check_policy(policy, [Stage(name="llm", kind="llm", endpoint=endpoint)])
    raw = _completion(
        endpoint=endpoint,
        messages=_messages(prompt, text, instructions),
        settings=settings,
        response_format={"type": "json_object"},
    )
    try:
        parsed = _json.loads(raw)
    except (_json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
        return {"_raw": raw}
    return parsed if isinstance(parsed, dict) else {"_raw": raw}

docs.title: Coolify Deployment (public hub)
docs.text:
The public hub runs on the ecsplico Coolify server from docker-compose.coolify.yml (Docker Compose build pack, Raw Compose Deployment on). It contains the hub and one internal live recognizer:

Service Image Listens Route hub ghcr.io/ecsplico/resona-hub@sha256:<digest> :7000 (expose only) https://resona-hub.ecsplico.de/* mcp same image, resona-mcp http :7010 (expose only) https://resona-hub.ecsplico.de/mcp engine-faster-whisper ghcr.io/ecsplico/resona-engine-faster-whisper@sha256:<digest> :7001 (expose only) none: internal, reached only by hub

There are no GPUs, Docker socket mounts, privileges or published ports. All containers run with a read-only root filesystem, all capabilities dropped and no-new-privileges; hub and mcp run as UID 1000, the engine as its image's root user with only its model cache volume hf-cache and /tmp writable. SQLite and the transient job payloads live on the named volume resona-data (/data); the database is never exposed. Queued jobs (uploads, documents, postprocessing) run on approved pull workers that connect outbound over HTTPS (Mac worker, Linux CUDA worker). When no worker is online, jobs wait in the queue. Live dictation (WS /v1/listen) does not go through workers: the hub bridges it to an engine-server, by default the internal engine-faster-whisper (Live recognizer).

TLS ends at Coolify's Caddy proxy. In raw mode Coolify adds no labels or networks, so the compose file declares the Caddy labels and the external coolify network itself.

docs.title: Hostnames and the PWA
docs.text:
• Hub + MCP: https://resona-hub.ecsplico.de.
  • PWA: https://resona.ecsplico.de, Coolify app resona-pwa (raw compose apps/resona-pwa/docker-compose.coolify.yml, base directory /apps/resona-pwa): Directus (SQLite volumes directus-db/directus-uploads), directus-bootstrap, pwa and project-worker. Directus has no public host: the PWA proxies an allow-list of its API paths at /directus/* (server/routes/directus/[...path].ts; no admin UI). Admin tasks run inside the container (docker exec <app-uuid>-directus-1 ...).
  • Login: Keycloak realm ecsplico through Directus' OpenID provider keycloak (Directus users are auto-created with the user role; password login stays as a fallback). Keycloak client resona-pwa (confidential, standard flow): redirect URI https://resona.ecsplico.de/directus/auth/login/keycloak/callback, web origin https://resona.ecsplico.de; its secret is the Coolify env KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET. Other required env: DIRECTUS_SECRET, DIRECTUS_TOKEN, DIRECTUS_ADMIN_*, DIRECTUS_USER_ROLE_ID, PWA_ORIGIN, NUXT_PUBLIC_DIRECTUS_URL=https://resona.ecsplico.de/directus, NUXT_PUBLIC_RESONA_API_URL, RESONA_API_URL, RESONA_API_KEY (client token of the ecsplico org, used by the project-worker).
  • Session length: Directus requests offline_access (AUTH_KEYCLOAK_SCOPE, override with KEYCLOAK_SCOPE) and refreshes the stored Keycloak token on every /auth/refresh (every ~15 min while the PWA is open). With an offline token the PWA session lasts until REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL (DIRECTUS_REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL, default 30d) of inactivity, instead of ending with the Keycloak SSO session (30 min idle / 10 h max). Realm admin, realm ecsplico:
  • Clients → resona-pwa → Client scopes: offline_access assigned (Optional is enough, Directus requests it). Settings: "Consent required" off.
  • Realm roles: offline_access stays in default-roles-ecsplico; users without that role get no offline token and the login fails.
  • Realm settings → Sessions: Offline Session Idle ≥ REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL (default 30 days fits). Leave "Offline Session Max Limited" off, or set Offline Session Max (e.g. 365 days) to force a yearly re-login.
  • Realm settings → Tokens: keep "Revoke Refresh Token" off (parallel refreshes from two tabs would revoke each other's token).
  • Takes effect at each user's next SSO login.
  • Logging out in the PWA does not end the Keycloak offline session: revoke it under Users → user → Sessions (Offline). Disabling a user in Keycloak ends their PWA session at the next refresh (≤ 15 min).
  • Encrypted off-site backups and the encryption-at-rest finding: PWA backups (compose profile backup).
  • Legacy: the hub also answers https://resona.ecsplico.de/v1/workers/* (a handle route in the compose labels) so workers still configured with the old origin keep working. Re-point them with --hub https://resona-hub.ecsplico.de, then remove the caddy_1* labels.

docs.title: Image
docs.text:
Every service runs a released image from GHCR, pinned by digest; the compose file has no build:, so Coolify only pulls. The GHCR packages are private. The Coolify host (<user>@<coolify-host>) holds a GitHub token with the single scope read:packages in /root/.docker/config.json (check with curl -sI -H "Authorization: token <t>" https://api.github.com/user | grep x-oauth-scopes), which Coolify's docker compose pull uses for both resona-hub and resona-engine-faster-whisper. Never put a token with wider scopes there. Should that token be revoked, pull the pinned digests from your own logged-in machine through the remote daemon instead of logging the server in: docker --host ssh://<user>@<coolify-host> pull ghcr.io/ecsplico/resona-hub@sha256:<digest> (likewise for the engine image; the client sends the credential per request; nothing is stored on the server) and add pull_policy: missing to the services so Compose skips the pull of a digest that is already present.

Bump per release:

  1. The release workflow (Releases) pushes ghcr.io/ecsplico/resona-hub:<version> and ghcr.io/ecsplico/resona-engine-faster-whisper:<version> and records their digests in release-manifest.json (images[].name).
  2. Replace the digest in both hub image: lines (hub, mcp) of docker-compose.coolify.yml and in the engine-faster-whisper image: line with those digests, update the Current … comment lines, commit and push to main.
  3. Deploy (below), then confirm the running digests: docker inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' <app-uuid>-hub-1 (and <app-uuid>-engine-faster-whisper-1) via a scheduled task on the host or the deployment log's pull lines.

Manual build outside the workflow (the first image, 0.1.0-d7405d3, was built this way): build from a clean git archive <commit> tree, never the working tree, docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 -f packages/api/Dockerfile -t ghcr.io/ecsplico/resona-hub:<version>-<commit> --push --metadata-file meta.json ., and pin containerimage.digest from meta.json. The Coolify server is amd64.
